regulatory.name: Food Safety Act 1990
regulatory.summary: Primary UK statute placing a duty on food businesses not to render food injurious to health, to ensure food is of the nature, substance, and quality demanded, and to label it accurately.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container produces fresh leafy greens for human consumption sold into the UK market; the operator is a food business under the Act and must not place unsafe food on the market.
regulatory.designImpact: All materials in contact with nutrient solution, growing media, or harvested crop (tanks, pipework, liners, rack surfaces) must be food-safe and non-contaminating; cleaning and disinfection protocols must be documented; no toxic substances (e.g., biocides, refrigerants) may contact the crop.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Food business registration with local authority Environmental Health Officer; documented HACCP plan covering biological, chemical, and physical hazards; material safety data sheets for all crop-contact materials confirming food-grade status.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as a food business with the relevant local authority before first harvest and commission a HACCP study covering the full growing and harvesting process inside the container.

regulatory.name: Regulation on the Hygiene of Foodstuffs (retained UK law)
regulatory.summary: Retained EU food hygiene regulation requiring food business operators to implement and maintain hygiene procedures based on HACCP principles.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Retained in UK law post-Brexit; applies to the production, handling, and dispatch of fresh produce from the container; operator must implement HACCP and maintain records.
regulatory.designImpact: Internal surfaces must be smooth, impervious, washable, and non-toxic (drives FRP/uPVC lining choice); floor bund must prevent cross-contamination from spills; hand-wash sink with potable water and air-gap backflow prevention is mandatory in the service vestibule; adequate lighting for inspection; pest exclusion at all penetrations.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written HACCP plan with hazard analysis, critical control points, monitoring records, and corrective action logs; local authority inspection sign-off; cleaning and disinfection schedule.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a food safety consultant to produce a HACCP plan aligned to the container layout before first commercial harvest.

regulatory.name: Food Processing Machinery — Basic Concepts — Part 2: Hygiene Requirements
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard specifying hygiene design requirements for food processing machinery, covering surface finish, drainability, cleanability, and material compatibility.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Grow racks, nutrient pipework, dosing systems, and harvesting bench constitute food processing machinery; compliance demonstrates conformity with the food hygiene obligations under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and the Food Safety Act 1990.
regulatory.designImpact: Rack frames must use food-zone and splash-zone materials (304 or 316 SS, anodised aluminium, or food-grade polymer); no crevices or dead-legs in pipework; all joints accessible for cleaning; floor sloped to drain; no cadmium, lead, or toxic coatings in crop-contact zones.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Design review report confirming compliance with BS EN 1672-2 hygiene zones; material certificates for all food-contact components; cleaning validation record.
regulatory.gapAction: Conduct a hygiene design review of rack, pipework, and tank layouts against BS EN 1672-2 food-zone and splash-zone requirements and document findings.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the UK market; requires risk assessment, technical file, and UKCA marking.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container contains automated machinery: circulation pumps, dosing pumps, HVAC fans, CO₂ solenoid valves, and a PLC-controlled nutrient dosing system; the integrated assembly constitutes a machinery assembly under the Regulations.
regulatory.designImpact: A machinery risk assessment per BS EN ISO 12100 must be completed; guards or interlocks required on rotating parts (pump impellers, fans); emergency stop provision for the automated nutrient and dosing system; safe isolation procedure documented; UKCA mark and Declaration of Conformity required before supply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Machinery technical file including risk assessment, design drawings, test records, and instructions for use; UKCA Declaration of Conformity; CE/UKCA mark on the assembly (UKCA for GB market).
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a machinery risk assessment per BS EN ISO 12100 covering all automated subsystems and begin compiling the technical file.

regulatory.name: Safety of Machinery — General Principles for Design — Risk Assessment and Risk Reduction
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard providing the methodology for machinery risk assessment and risk reduction by design, safeguarding, and information.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Demonstrates compliance with the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 for the integrated automated systems (pumps, fans, dosing, CO₂ solenoids) within the container.
regulatory.designImpact: Three-step hierarchy (inherently safe design, safeguarding, information) must be applied to each hazard identified; residual risks documented in instructions for use; emergency stop and isolation points sized and located per the risk assessment outcome.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Completed risk assessment document referencing BS EN ISO 12100 methodology, signed by a competent person; included in the machinery technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Use BS EN ISO 12100 as the framework for the machinery risk assessment; assign a competent mechanical engineer to lead the study.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC to be safe and to meet essential safety requirements before being placed on the market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container's entire electrical installation (main distribution board, LED drivers, HVAC compressor, pumps, PLC, sensor nodes) operates at 400 V three-phase and 230 V single-phase; the integrated electrical assembly must satisfy the essential safety requirements before supply.
regulatory.designImpact: All electrical equipment must be selected, installed, and tested to prevent hazards from electric shock, fire, and mechanical danger; equipment must carry appropriate conformity marking; the distribution board, RCDs, and wiring must comply with BS 7671; IP ratings must be appropriate for the wet agricultural environment (minimum IP54 for enclosures, IP67 for mains inlet).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the electrical assembly; electrical installation certificate (EIC) per BS 7671; test certificates for individual equipment items; IP rating certificates for enclosures.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm all electrical equipment selections carry valid conformity marking and commission an EIC from a qualified electrician after installation.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument placing duties on employers and employees to ensure electrical systems are constructed, maintained, and used safely.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to the three-phase 400 V installation inside the container and to any person working on or near it; the operator has a duty to maintain the electrical system in a safe condition and to ensure work on live systems is only done where unavoidable.
regulatory.designImpact: Isolation and lock-off provisions must be designed in for each sub-circuit; safe working procedures for maintenance of the distribution board, LED drivers, and pump panels must be documented; periodic inspection and testing schedule must be established.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written safe system of work for electrical maintenance; periodic inspection and test report (PITR) at intervals determined by a competent person; records of all electrical maintenance activities.
regulatory.gapAction: Establish an electrical maintenance schedule and safe isolation procedure; arrange first periodic inspection after commissioning.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations governing the design, installation, inspection, and testing of fixed electrical installations.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal fixed wiring, distribution board, RCDs, circuit protection, earthing, and bonding within the container; compliance demonstrates conformity with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: All circuits must have 30 mA Type-A RCD protection given the wet agricultural environment; equipotential bonding to all metallic water pipework, rack frames, and tank; minimum IP ratings for accessories in wet zones (IP44 minimum, IP65 preferred at canopy level); cable selection for ambient temperature uplift from LED heat load; main switch and isolation per Section 537.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical installation certificate (EIC) with schedule of inspections and test results, signed by a qualified person; minor works certificates for any subsequent modifications.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a qualified electrical designer to produce a BS 7671-compliant circuit schedule and specification before wiring commences.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to be designed so that electromagnetic disturbance generated does not exceed levels allowing other equipment to operate as intended, and that the apparatus has adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container's LED drivers (switched-mode power supplies), PLC, 4G/IoT gateway, variable-speed HVAC drives, and dosing pump controllers are all potential EMC emission sources; the integrated assembly must meet essential EMC requirements before supply.
regulatory.designImpact: LED drivers and variable-speed drives must be selected with EMC filters; cable routing must segregate power and signal cables; the PLC and IoT gateway must have adequate immunity to conducted and radiated disturbance from the LED and HVAC loads; EMC assessment or testing required for the integrated assembly.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity citing EMC compliance; EMC test report or technical construction file with EMC assessment for the integrated assembly; CE/UKCA marks on individual apparatus.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify all emission sources (LED drivers, VSD, PLC) and confirm each has EMC conformity marking; commission an EMC assessment for the integrated container assembly.

regulatory.code: IET Code of Practice for Electrical Installations in Agricultural and Horticultural Premises
regulatory.name: IET Code of Practice for Electrical Installations in Agricultural and Horticultural Premises
regulatory.summary: IET guidance on applying BS 7671 to the specific hazards of agricultural and horticultural environments, including wet conditions, corrosive atmospheres, and livestock/crop proximity.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — The container is a horticultural production environment with high humidity, nutrient solution spray, and condensation; this Code of Practice supplements BS 7671 with sector-specific guidance endorsed by HSE.
regulatory.designImpact: Enhanced IP ratings throughout (IP65 minimum at canopy level); corrosion-resistant cable management (stainless or PVC-coated trunking); additional RCD protection tiers; increased inspection frequency; avoidance of aluminium conductors in corrosive zones.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Design review confirming compliance with the Code of Practice recommendations; noted in the EIC supplementary schedule.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain the IET Code of Practice and cross-reference the electrical design against its agricultural/horticultural-specific requirements before finalising the circuit schedule.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety statute placing general duties on employers to ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health, safety, and welfare of employees and others affected by their work.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to all persons entering or working in the container (weekly transplanting staff, maintenance engineers, delivery personnel); the operator must assess and control risks from electrical hazards, CO₂ asphyxiation, manual handling, working in confined spaces, and chemical handling (nutrient concentrates, pH adjustment acids/alkalis).
regulatory.designImpact: CO₂ concentration monitoring with audible/visual alarm and automatic dosing cut-off if CO₂ exceeds 5,000 ppm (TWA) or 15,000 ppm (STEL) per WEL; confined-space risk assessment for entry procedures; chemical storage and handling provisions for pH acids/alkalis; manual handling assessment for rack loading and reservoir maintenance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written COSHH assessment for CO₂, nutrient concentrates, and pH chemicals; confined-space risk assessment and entry procedure; manual handling assessment; CO₂ alarm test records.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a COSHH assessment and confined-space risk assessment before first staffed operation; install CO₂ alarm with automatic dosing interlock.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument placing duties on clients, designers, and contractors for health and safety during construction, installation, and maintenance of structures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Site installation of the container (foundation preparation, mains electrical connection, water supply connection) constitutes construction work; CDM applies if the work lasts more than 30 working days with more than 20 workers simultaneously, or exceeds 500 person-days; even below these thresholds, designer and contractor duties apply.
regulatory.designImpact: Designer must consider safe installation sequence, maintenance access (aisle width, roof access for HVAC), and safe future demolition; principal contractor must produce a construction phase plan; health and safety file must be handed to the client on completion.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: CDM notification to HSE (F10) if thresholds exceeded; construction phase plan; health and safety file including as-built drawings, maintenance instructions, and test records.
regulatory.gapAction: Assess whether each installation project meets CDM notification thresholds; brief the installation contractor on CDM duties and require a construction phase plan.

regulatory.code: UKCA Marking (Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019)
regulatory.name: UKCA Marking Regulations (umbrella scheme)
regulatory.summary: UK conformity assessment marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the Great Britain market, covering multiple product directives including machinery, electrical equipment, EMC, and radio equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container as a whole, and its constituent electrical and mechanical sub-assemblies, must carry UKCA marking before being placed on the GB market; this is the umbrella obligation under which the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016, and Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 all sit.
regulatory.designImpact: A single UKCA Declaration of Conformity covering all applicable regulations must be produced; technical files must be compiled and retained for 10 years; UKCA mark must be affixed to the product (or its packaging/documentation if the product is too small).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity listing all applicable regulations and designated standards; technical files for each regulatory regime; UKCA mark affixed to the container.
regulatory.gapAction: Map all applicable regulations to the UKCA umbrella and assign a responsible person to compile and sign the Declaration of Conformity before first supply.

regulatory.name: General Product Safety Regulations 2005
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring all consumer products placed on the market to be safe; applies as a backstop where no specific product safety legislation covers a hazard.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies as a backstop to any hazard not covered by the specific machinery, electrical, or food safety regulations; relevant to the container as a product supplied to food business operators who are not necessarily technical specialists.
regulatory.designImpact: Residual risks not addressed by specific regulations must be assessed and mitigated; instructions for use must be clear and in English; warnings for CO₂ asphyxiation, electrical isolation, and chemical handling must be provided; product must be safe in foreseeable misuse.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk assessment covering residual hazards; instructions for use in English; records of any safety-related product modifications or recalls.
regulatory.gapAction: Review residual hazards after specific-regulation compliance is established and confirm GPSR backstop obligations are met; include safety warnings in the operator manual.

regulatory.name: Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring water fittings to be installed so as to prevent waste, misuse, undue consumption, erroneous measurement, or contamination of the public water supply.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container connects to a mains potable water supply for the hand-wash sink and nutrient system top-up; backflow prevention is mandatory to protect the public supply from contamination by nutrient solution (a fluid category 4 or 5 risk).
regulatory.designImpact: A Type AA air gap (minimum 20 mm) must be provided at the point of mains water entry to the nutrient reservoir; no direct connection between the mains supply and the recirculating nutrient system is permissible; WRAS-approved fittings and materials must be used throughout the potable water circuit.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WRAS approval certificates for all fittings in the potable water circuit; installation notification to the water undertaker (required for fluid category 4/5 risk); inspection by water undertaker if required.
regulatory.gapAction: Notify the local water undertaker of the installation and confirm the backflow prevention strategy (Type AA air gap) meets the fluid category risk; specify only WRAS-approved fittings.

regulatory.name: The Fluorinated Greenhouse Gases Regulations 2015 (as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the use, recovery, and reporting of fluorinated greenhouse gases including HFC refrigerants used in refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The HVAC/dehumidification system uses R32 or R454B refrigerant (both F-gases); the operator has duties for leak checking, record keeping, and ensuring only F-Gas certified engineers service the refrigerant circuit.
regulatory.designImpact: Refrigerant charge must be minimised; system must be leak-tested before commissioning and at intervals determined by charge size; refrigerant type and charge weight must be labelled on the unit; only F-Gas certified technicians may handle refrigerant.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: F-Gas leak check records; refrigerant logbook; F-Gas certification of servicing engineers; equipment label showing refrigerant type and charge.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm HVAC supplier provides F-Gas compliant equipment with labelling; establish a refrigerant logbook and engage an F-Gas certified engineer for commissioning and servicing.

regulatory.code: Biocidal Products Regulation (UK BPR) (SI 2001/880 as retained and amended)
regulatory.name: UK Biocidal Products Regulation
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the authorisation and use of biocidal products, including disinfectants and algaecides used in water systems.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Any disinfectant, algaecide, or sterilant used to clean the nutrient reservoir, pipework, or growing channels is a biocidal product and must be authorised under UK BPR; the UV steriliser is not a biocidal product but chemical sterilants are.
regulatory.designImpact: Only UK BPR-authorised biocidal products may be used; product labels must be followed; residue management must ensure no biocide contamination of the crop; COSHH assessment required for each biocidal product used.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UK BPR authorisation numbers for all biocidal products used; COSHH assessments; cleaning records confirming correct dilution and contact time; evidence of residue clearance before replanting.
regulatory.gapAction: Compile a list of all cleaning and disinfection chemicals intended for use; confirm each holds UK BPR authorisation and include in the COSHH assessment.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Specification and Testing — Part 1: General Cargo Containers for General Purposes
regulatory.summary: International standard specifying structural requirements and test methods for ISO series 1 freight containers; the basis for the CSC plate certification.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — The 40HC container shell is the structural chassis; the original CSC plate is voided once the shell is structurally modified by cutting penetrations for HVAC ducts, electrical conduit, CO₂ supply, and water connections. Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is required; ISO 1496-1 is not UK statute but loss of CSC certification has insurance and transport consequences.
regulatory.designImpact: All penetrations through the container shell (HVAC, electrical inlet, water, CO₂) must be assessed for their effect on structural integrity; a finite element analysis or equivalent structural calculation must demonstrate that the modified container meets the original load cases (stacking, racking, lifting); the original CSC plate must be removed or defaced once modifications are made.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Structural calculation pack or FEA report for the modified container demonstrating compliance with the original ISO 1496-1 load cases; new structural certification from a recognised classification society or competent structural engineer; updated container identification plate.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a structural engineer to assess the impact of all planned shell penetrations and produce a calculation pack; engage a classification society (e.g., Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas) for re-certification if required for transport or insurance.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring pressure systems to be designed, installed, maintained, and operated safely; applies to systems containing a relevant fluid above certain pressure and volume thresholds.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The CO₂ supply system (47 L cylinder at up to 200 bar, reducing to working pressure) and the closed-loop nutrient pipework (PN10 rated) constitute pressure systems; PSSR applies to the CO₂ cylinder and regulator assembly as a pressure system in service.
regulatory.designImpact: A written scheme of examination must be produced for the CO₂ pressure system by a competent person; the CO₂ cylinder must be inspected at prescribed intervals; pressure relief devices must be fitted and maintained; the nutrient pipework, if below the PSSR threshold, must still be designed to PN10 and pressure-tested before commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written scheme of examination for the CO₂ pressure system; inspection records; pressure test certificate for nutrient pipework; competent person sign-off.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a competent person (e.g., an insurer's engineer or specialist contractor) to produce a written scheme of examination for the CO₂ system before commissioning.

regulatory.code: Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/2776)
regulatory.name: Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring employers to assess and control risks from fire and explosion arising from dangerous substances, including flammable gases and dusts.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — CO₂ is an asphyxiant rather than flammable, so DSEAR's explosion provisions do not apply to CO₂ itself; however, if any flammable cleaning solvents or nutrient additives are stored in the container, DSEAR applies; the assessment must confirm no ATEX zone is created inside the container.
regulatory.designImpact: A DSEAR risk assessment must confirm that no flammable atmosphere can arise inside the container; if any flammable substance is used, zoning, equipment selection, and ignition source control must be addressed; CO₂ asphyxiation risk is addressed under COSHH/HSWA rather than DSEAR.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: DSEAR risk assessment confirming no explosive atmosphere; if flammable substances are present, ATEX zone drawing and equipment schedule.
regulatory.gapAction: Complete a DSEAR risk assessment covering all substances stored and used in the container; confirm no flammable atmosphere risk and document the finding.

regulatory.name: Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring employers to avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable and to assess and reduce risk where it cannot be avoided.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Weekly transplanting operations involve repetitive handling of plant trays, nutrient concentrate containers (up to 25 L), and CO₂ cylinders (up to 50 kg full); the 700–900 mm aisle width constrains posture during rack loading.
regulatory.designImpact: Rack tier height must be designed so that the highest planting position is reachable without overhead stretching beyond safe limits; CO₂ cylinder change-out must be achievable with mechanical assistance or by two persons; nutrient concentrate containers must be sized to remain within single-person lift limits (≤25 kg); aisle width must accommodate safe working posture.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Manual handling risk assessment covering transplanting, CO₂ cylinder change, and nutrient concentrate handling; records of any task redesign to reduce risk.
regulatory.gapAction: Conduct a manual handling risk assessment during the design phase, focusing on rack tier reach heights and CO₂ cylinder handling; adjust design if any task exceeds acceptable risk levels.

regulatory.code: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/2677)
regulatory.name: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring employers to assess and control exposure to hazardous substances, including chemicals and biological agents.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Nutrient concentrate solutions (containing nitrates, phosphates, and micronutrients), pH adjustment acids and alkalis, CO₂ (asphyxiant at elevated concentrations), and potential biological agents (Legionella in recirculating water systems) are all hazardous substances present in the container.
regulatory.designImpact: CO₂ dosing system must have automatic cut-off and alarm at safe exposure limits; pH acid/alkali storage must be in secondary containment; Legionella risk assessment required for the recirculating nutrient system (warm water, potential aerosol from spray nozzles); PPE requirements for chemical handling must be specified in operating procedures.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: COSHH assessment for each hazardous substance; Legionella risk assessment and written control scheme; PPE specification; training records for operators.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a COSHH assessment covering all chemicals and biological hazards before first operation; include Legionella risk assessment for the recirculating nutrient system.

regulatory.name: UK General Data Protection Regulation and Data Protection Act 2018
regulatory.summary: UK data protection law governing the collection, processing, storage, and transfer of personal data.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The IoT sensor mesh and remote farm-management dashboard collect operational data; if any data is linked to named individuals (operator accounts, access logs, location data), UK GDPR applies; the cloud dashboard provider relationship must be governed by a data processing agreement.
regulatory.designImpact: Dashboard user accounts must be protected with appropriate access controls; data minimisation principle applies — only data necessary for farm management should be collected; data retention periods must be defined; if the dashboard is hosted outside the UK, international transfer safeguards apply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Privacy notice for dashboard users; data processing agreement with cloud hosting provider; ICO registration (if required); records of processing activities.
regulatory.gapAction: Assess whether personal data is processed via the dashboard; if so, register with the ICO, produce a privacy notice, and put a data processing agreement in place with the cloud provider.

regulatory.code: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring producers of electrical and electronic equipment to finance the collection, treatment, and recycling of waste EEE.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The container contains electrical and electronic equipment (LED drivers, PLC, IoT sensor nodes, dosing pump controllers, HVAC controls) placed on the GB market; the producer must register with an approved WEEE compliance scheme.
regulatory.designImpact: Equipment must be designed for disassembly and recycling where practicable; WEEE marking (crossed-out wheelie bin) must appear on electrical equipment; producer registration and compliance scheme membership required before first supply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration number; compliance scheme membership certificate; WEEE marking on equipment.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as a WEEE producer with an approved compliance scheme before first supply of the container.

regulatory.name: Restriction of Hazardous Substances Regulations 2012
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument restricting the use of certain hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, and four phthalates) in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical and electronic equipment within the container (LED bars, drivers, PLC, sensor nodes, pump controllers) placed on the GB market must comply with RoHS substance restrictions.
regulatory.designImpact: Component selection must exclude RoHS-restricted substances; suppliers must provide RoHS declarations of conformity; particular attention to LED phosphor and driver PCB materials.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity for each electrical/electronic sub-assembly; supplier RoHS declarations for components; technical documentation confirming substance compliance.
regulatory.gapAction: Require RoHS declarations from all electrical component suppliers and compile into the technical file before first supply.

regulatory.name: Photobiological Safety of Lamps and Lamp Systems
regulatory.summary: Standard specifying photobiological safety requirements and test methods for lamps and lamp systems, including LED grow-lights, covering UV, blue-light, and IR hazard groups.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — The 140–170 full-spectrum horticultural LED bars emit significant blue-light and potentially UV radiation at close working distances during transplanting and maintenance; photobiological hazard assessment is required to determine the risk group and any necessary exposure limits or warnings.
regulatory.designImpact: LED bars must be assessed for blue-light hazard (retinal) and UV hazard (skin/eye) at the working distances encountered during transplanting (operator face within 500–800 mm of canopy-level fixtures); if Risk Group 2 or above, warning labels and restricted viewing distances must be specified in the operator manual; eye protection may be required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Photobiological safety assessment report per BS EN 62471 for the LED bar type selected; risk group classification; warning labels on fixtures if required; PPE specification in operator manual.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain photobiological safety data sheet from the LED bar supplier; if Risk Group 2 or above, commission a formal BS EN 62471 assessment and specify appropriate warnings and PPE.

regulatory.code: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (SI 1998/2306)
regulatory.name: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring work equipment to be suitable, maintained, and used safely, with adequate guarding, controls, and information.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All equipment provided for use by workers in the container (circulation pumps, dosing pumps, HVAC fans, UV steriliser, transplant bench tools) is work equipment under PUWER; the operator must ensure it is suitable, maintained, and that workers are trained in its safe use.
regulatory.designImpact: Dangerous parts (pump impellers, fan blades) must be guarded; controls must be clearly identified and accessible; equipment must be maintained in good repair; maintenance records must be kept; workers must receive adequate training and information.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: PUWER risk assessment for each item of work equipment; maintenance schedule and records; training records for operators; guard inspection records.
regulatory.gapAction: Produce a PUWER assessment for all work equipment in the container and establish a maintenance schedule before first staffed operation.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Low Voltage Directive for electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC; requires UKCA marking and a technical file.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Mains-powered variant of Hedgerow (optional mains supply for low-light gardens) falls squarely within scope; the solar-only variant with LiFePO4 battery operating at low voltage must be assessed for whether output voltages cross the LVD threshold, but the mains input variant is unambiguously in scope.
regulatory.designImpact: Mains variant must achieve basic insulation, double insulation or protective earth, and safe disconnection; technical file must include risk assessment, circuit diagrams, and test results against a designated standard (BS EN 60335-1 or BS EN 62368-1 as applicable).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing the designated standard; technical file retained for 10 years; test report from accredited or in-house competent body.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine whether solar-only variant output voltages are below LVD threshold; commission LVD assessment for mains variant against BS EN 62368-1 or BS EN 60335-1 and open technical file.

regulatory.name: Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206) — UK RED
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring radio equipment to be safe, electromagnetically compatible, and use spectrum efficiently; applies to any product with an intentional radio transmitter.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow contains Wi-Fi (2.4/5 GHz), optional cellular (LTE-M/NB-IoT), and LoRa (868 MHz UK ISM) transmitters; all three radio interfaces trigger RED obligations. Pre-certified radio modules carry their own RED compliance but the host product (Hedgerow as a system) must still demonstrate that integration does not invalidate module certification.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna placement, radome design (steel body variant), and inter-antenna isolation (≥λ/4 at 868 MHz ≈ 86 mm) must be validated; host integration test required even with pre-certified modules; LoRa must operate within Ofcom IR 2030 duty-cycle and EIRP limits for 868 MHz.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity citing Radio Equipment Regulations 2017; antenna integration test report; if pre-certified module used, supplier DoC plus host integration evidence; Ofcom IR 2030 compliance statement for LoRa.
regulatory.gapAction: Select pre-certified Wi-Fi/BLE and LoRa modules; commission antenna integration test on steel-body prototype; confirm LoRa duty-cycle parameters comply with Ofcom IR 2030.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring apparatus to not cause harmful electromagnetic interference and to have adequate immunity; applies to all electrical/electronic apparatus placed on the UK market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow as a complete product (camera, NPU SoC, PMIC, sensors, radio modules) must meet EMC emission and immunity limits; steel body may act as a partial Faraday cage aiding emissions but apertures for camera, microphone, and radome will require careful EMC management.
regulatory.designImpact: PCB layout must minimise radiated emissions from NPU and camera interface; cable routing and connector shielding required; immunity testing (ESD, conducted disturbance, surge for mains variant) must be passed; steel body apertures sized to avoid slot antenna effects at operating frequencies.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report (CISPR 32 emissions, EN 55035 immunity or equivalent) from UKAS-accredited test house; UKCA DoC citing EMC Regulations 2016.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage EMC test house early in PCB design phase; conduct pre-compliance scan on first prototype; book formal EMC chamber time for production-representative sample.

regulatory.name: UKCA Marking Obligations (Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and successor SIs)
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK conformity marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the Great Britain market; required across multiple product regulations simultaneously.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow must carry UKCA marking as it is placed on the GB market and falls under at least three concurrent statutory regimes (Radio Equipment Regulations 2017, Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016); a single UKCA mark covers all applicable regulations provided each technical file is complete.
regulatory.designImpact: UKCA mark must be affixed to the product (or packaging if product too small); Declaration of Conformity must list all applicable regulations; technical files for each regime must be maintained for 10 years; UK Responsible Person address required on product or packaging.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity listing all applicable regulations; technical files for each regime; UK Responsible Person designation if manufacturer is outside GB.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint UK Responsible Person; draft master DoC template listing all applicable regulations; establish document control system for technical files.

regulatory.name: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (SI 2005/1803) — GPSR
regulatory.summary: UK statutory baseline safety obligation for all consumer products not covered by a specific product safety directive; requires products to be safe and imposes recall/withdrawal duties.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is a consumer product sold to members of the public; GPSR applies as a backstop safety obligation across all variants (solar-only and mains); outdoor use in gardens with potential child and pet access heightens the duty of care.
regulatory.designImpact: Formal risk assessment required covering all foreseeable use and misuse scenarios (child access to battery compartment, ingestion of small parts, perch structural failure, water ingress to live parts); post-market surveillance plan required; traceability markings (batch/serial) required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk assessment document; post-market surveillance procedure; incident reporting procedure; product recall plan.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission consumer product risk assessment covering outdoor use, child access, and battery safety; establish post-market surveillance and incident reporting procedures before first sale.

regulatory.name: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 — IoT Security Requirements
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring consumer connectable products to meet minimum cybersecurity requirements; commenced 29 April 2024.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is a consumer connectable product with Wi-Fi, optional cellular, and LoRa connectivity; all three radio interfaces make it a 'connectable product' under the Act; the companion app and cloud backend are in scope for the security requirements.
regulatory.designImpact: No default or universal passwords permitted; must publish a vulnerability disclosure policy with a public point of contact; must declare minimum security update support period to consumers; firmware update mechanism must be authenticated and integrity-checked; these requirements apply from first sale.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Statement of compliance with PSTI Act 2022 Schedule 1 requirements; published vulnerability disclosure policy URL; security update support period declaration in product documentation; internal evidence of password policy and update mechanism design.
regulatory.gapAction: Implement unique per-device credentials or user-set password at onboarding; publish vulnerability disclosure policy; define and document minimum security update support period; engage security consultant to review firmware update chain.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument restricting lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE, and four phthalates in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is electrical and electronic equipment placed on the UK market; all PCBs, solder, cables, connectors, and plastic components must comply with RoHS substance limits; ceramic glaze and powder coating must be assessed for hexavalent chromium and cadmium content.
regulatory.designImpact: Lead-free solder required throughout; powder coating formulation must be RoHS-compliant (no hexavalent chromium); ceramic glaze must be assessed for cadmium and lead content; supplier declarations required for all components.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity; supplier RoHS declarations for all components and materials; test reports for any materials where substance content is uncertain (ceramic glaze, powder coating).
regulatory.gapAction: Issue RoHS compliance questionnaire to all component and material suppliers; obtain glaze and powder coating formulation data sheets and assess against RoHS limits; include RoHS DoC in UKCA technical file.

regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring producers of EEE to fund collection, treatment, and recycling of waste electrical equipment; requires registration with an approved producer compliance scheme.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow is EEE placed on the UK market; the founder is a producer and must register with an approved WEEE compliance scheme before first sale; the LiFePO4 battery is separately subject to battery waste regulations.
regulatory.designImpact: Product must be marked with the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol; packaging must include WEEE take-back information; product design should facilitate disassembly for recycling (accessible battery, separable PCBs).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration number from approved compliance scheme; annual WEEE data submission records; crossed-out wheelie bin marking on product.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK-approved WEEE compliance scheme (e.g. Valpak, Recolight) before first sale; add WEEE symbol to product and packaging artwork; design battery compartment for tool-accessible removal.

regulatory.name: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/890) as amended
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the placing on the market of batteries and accumulators; restricts mercury and cadmium content and requires producer registration for battery waste collection.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow contains a LiFePO4 battery pack; the founder is a battery producer and must register with a battery compliance scheme; end-of-life battery take-back obligations apply.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery must be removable by the end user or at a collection point (or justification provided why not); battery must be marked with capacity and chemistry; crossed-out wheelie bin symbol required on battery or product.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Battery producer registration with approved compliance scheme; battery marking evidence; take-back information in user documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK battery compliance scheme; confirm LiFePO4 cell cadmium and mercury content is within limits; design battery compartment for accessible removal; add battery markings to artwork.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium Batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory international transport safety test protocol for lithium cells and batteries; required before any shipment by road, sea, or air.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LiFePO4 battery cells and assembled pack during transport from manufacturer to UK; governed by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs) for road, IMDG Code for sea, and IATA DGR for air freight; UN 38.3 test summary is a prerequisite for all modes.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack design (cell count, series/parallel configuration, protection circuit) must be finalised before UN 38.3 testing; any design change to the pack after certification may require re-testing; pack must include protection against overcharge, over-discharge, and short circuit.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell supplier or accredited test laboratory covering the specific cell and pack configuration used in Hedgerow; dangerous goods documentation for each shipment mode.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm cell supplier holds valid UN 38.3 certification for the selected LiFePO4 cell; obtain test summary report; prepare dangerous goods documentation template for inbound shipments.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells, and for batteries made from them, for use in portable applications — Part 2: Lithium systems
regulatory.summary: Designated standard for safety of lithium battery packs in portable/consumer applications; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the battery subsystem.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LiFePO4 battery pack within Hedgerow (portable consumer product); demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the battery subsystem; serves the UKCA Low Voltage scheme for the battery.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack must pass cell-level and pack-level abuse tests (overcharge, forced discharge, short circuit, crush, thermal abuse); protection circuit design must meet the standard's requirements; pack must be tested as a complete assembly in its final configuration.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 62133-2 test report from UKAS-accredited laboratory covering the final pack configuration; supplier cell-level test data.
regulatory.gapAction: Select LiFePO4 cells with existing IEC 62133-2 cell-level data; design protection circuit; commission pack-level testing at UKAS-accredited lab once pack design is frozen.

regulatory.name: Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment — Part 1: Safety requirements
regulatory.summary: Designated standard for safety of AV/IT/ICT equipment; the preferred designated standard for complex consumer electronics combining power, computing, and communications.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Hedgerow's NPU SoC, camera, connectivity modules, and power management electronics constitute ICT/AV equipment; BS EN 62368-1 is the appropriate designated standard to demonstrate compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the electronics subsystem (mains and solar-powered variants).
regulatory.designImpact: Hazard-based safety engineering (HBSE) approach required; energy source classification (ES1/ES2/ES3) for battery and mains circuits; safeguard requirements for each energy source; creepage and clearance distances for mains variant; thermal limits for NPU and battery.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 62368-1 test report from UKAS-accredited laboratory or competent in-house body; thermal test data for NPU under worst-case ambient; creepage/clearance calculation pack for mains variant.
regulatory.gapAction: Classify all energy sources per BS EN 62368-1 Annex A; conduct thermal assessment of NPU SoC at maximum ambient; commission formal safety testing against BS EN 62368-1 on production-representative prototype.

regulatory.name: Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)
regulatory.summary: Designated standard defining ingress protection ratings for enclosures against solid particles and liquids; used to substantiate outdoor suitability claims.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Hedgerow is an outdoor product exposed to UK weather year-round; IP rating substantiates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 and GPSR for outdoor electrical safety; minimum IP54 recommended for body, IP65 for sensor and connector apertures.
regulatory.designImpact: Enclosure design must achieve and maintain the target IP rating after assembly, including all apertures (camera window, microphone port, sensor ports, charging connector, reservoir interface); gasket and seal design is critical; IP rating must be maintained after repeated reservoir removal and refitting.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: IP test report from UKAS-accredited laboratory on production-representative enclosure; seal durability assessment after repeated reservoir cycling.
regulatory.gapAction: Define target IP rating for each zone of the enclosure; design gaskets and seals; commission IP54/IP65 ingress protection testing on first production-representative prototype.

regulatory.name: Photobiological safety of lamps and lamp systems
regulatory.summary: Standard assessing photobiological hazard of optical radiation sources; applies to any product with LEDs or illuminated optical systems.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Hedgerow's 12 MP camera with optical zoom may include an IR illuminator or status LEDs; if any LED or illuminated element is present, photobiological safety assessment is required; optical zoom lens system must be assessed if it concentrates light toward the user's eye during setup or maintenance.
regulatory.designImpact: Any IR illuminator or LED must be classified into a risk group (exempt, RG1, RG2, RG3); RG2 or above requires warnings and may require design changes to limit exposure; camera lens must not concentrate solar radiation to a hazardous level during installation.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Photobiological safety assessment report classifying all optical sources; if RG1 or above, risk group marking and user warnings in documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify all LEDs and optical sources in the design; commission photobiological safety assessment per BS EN IEC 62471; if IR illuminator is included, confirm RG classification and add appropriate warnings.

regulatory.name: UK General Data Protection Regulation and Data Protection Act 2018
regulatory.summary: UK statutory framework governing the collection, processing, and storage of personal data; applies to any product or service that processes data relating to identified or identifiable individuals.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow's camera captures video of gardens which may incidentally record people (neighbours, visitors); the companion app processes individual bird identification data linked to user accounts; the citizen-science BTO data contribution toggle involves data sharing with a third party; all constitute personal data processing under UK GDPR.
regulatory.designImpact: Privacy by design required: on-device processing preferred over cloud upload of raw video; user consent mechanism required for citizen-science data sharing; data minimisation for BTO contribution (species/location/time only, no identifiable imagery); data retention limits; right to erasure implementation in app and backend; privacy notice required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) for camera and citizen-science data flows; privacy notice published; ICO registration (if required); data processing agreement with BTO; record of processing activities.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission DPIA covering camera data, individual bird identification profiles, and BTO data sharing; draft privacy notice; negotiate data processing agreement with BTO; register with ICO if annual turnover or processing scale triggers obligation.

regulatory.name: Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (SI 2003/2426)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing electronic communications, cookies, and direct marketing; applies to connected devices and companion apps that use cookies or send marketing communications.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow companion app uses network communications and may set cookies or similar tracking technologies; push notifications for daily highlight reels and marketing communications require PECR-compliant consent; cellular add-on service involves electronic communications.
regulatory.designImpact: App must obtain explicit consent before setting non-essential cookies or tracking; push notification opt-in must be granular (highlight reel vs marketing); unsubscribe mechanism required for all electronic marketing.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Consent management mechanism in app; cookie/tracking policy; records of consent; legal review of push notification flows.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage data protection solicitor to review app consent flows against PECR; implement consent management platform in app; draft cookie and tracking policy.

regulatory.name: Ofcom Interface Requirement 2030 — UK 868 MHz Short Range Devices
regulatory.summary: Ofcom licence-exempt spectrum authorisation for short-range devices operating in the 868 MHz band; sets EIRP limits and duty-cycle restrictions for LoRa and similar technologies.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Hedgerow's LoRa mesh operates at 868 MHz UK ISM band; Ofcom IR 2030 defines the licence-exempt conditions (typically 25 mW EIRP, 1% duty cycle for 868.0–868.6 MHz sub-band) that must be met for lawful operation without a licence.
regulatory.designImpact: LoRa firmware must enforce duty-cycle limits per IR 2030 sub-band allocations; EIRP must not exceed 25 mW (14 dBm) in the relevant sub-band; antenna gain must be accounted for in EIRP calculation; mesh protocol must not cause aggregate duty-cycle violations across multiple feeders.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: LoRa module EIRP and duty-cycle specification from supplier; firmware duty-cycle enforcement documentation; antenna gain data sheet; RED compliance evidence for LoRa module.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm LoRa module EIRP and duty-cycle parameters against IR 2030 sub-band limits; implement firmware duty-cycle enforcement; document aggregate duty-cycle behaviour for multi-feeder mesh scenarios.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the UK market; applies to products with moving parts driven by other than direct human or animal effort.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Hedgerow's motorised optical zoom mechanism (if motor-driven) and any automated reservoir dispensing mechanism constitute machinery under the Regulations; assessment required to determine whether the zoom actuator triggers full machinery scope or is excluded as a simple actuator within an EEE product.
regulatory.designImpact: If in scope: CE/UKCA machinery marking required; harmonised standard BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment required; guarding of any pinch points in zoom mechanism; if excluded from Machinery Regs as EEE, safety is covered under Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 instead.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Machinery scope determination memo; if in scope: UKCA machinery DoC, BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment, technical file; if excluded: documented rationale.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine whether motorised zoom and any automated mechanisms trigger Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 scope; document determination; if in scope, commission BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations for fixed electrical installations; applies to the mains-powered variant's installation wiring from the consumer unit to the outdoor socket or direct connection point.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Mains-powered variant of Hedgerow requires an outdoor electrical installation (garden socket or direct wiring); BS 7671 governs the fixed installation from the consumer unit to the point of connection; relevant chapters include outdoor installations, RCD protection for outdoor circuits, and cable burial depth if applicable.
regulatory.designImpact: Mains variant must be designed for connection to a BS 7671-compliant outdoor circuit with RCD protection (30 mA Type A minimum); product documentation must specify installation requirements; if Hedgerow includes a fixed cable for direct connection, cable specification must meet BS 7671 outdoor requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Installation instructions specifying BS 7671 outdoor circuit requirements; if product includes fixed wiring, cable specification and installation guidance; installer competence requirement stated in documentation.
regulatory.gapAction: Draft mains variant installation instructions specifying outdoor RCD-protected circuit requirement per BS 7671 Chapter 41 and Section 714; specify minimum cable rating and IP rating for outdoor connection.

regulatory.name: ISTA Test Procedure 3A — Packaged Products for Parcel Delivery System Shipment
regulatory.summary: Voluntary packaging performance standard for direct-to-consumer parcel shipments up to 70 kg; tests atmospheric preconditioning, vibration, and drop sequences representative of parcel carrier handling.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Hedgerow will be shipped direct-to-consumer via parcel carriers; ISTA 3A is the industry-standard packaging validation protocol used by major UK carriers and retailers as a condition of listing; ceramic body variant is particularly vulnerable to transit damage.
regulatory.designImpact: Packaging must protect ceramic or steel body, solar panel, and modular reservoirs through ISTA 3A drop and vibration sequences; internal cushioning design (foam profile, void fill) must be validated; ceramic body requires more robust cushioning than steel variant.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: ISTA 3A test report on production-representative packaged product; separate test reports for ceramic and steel body variants if packaging differs.
regulatory.gapAction: Design packaging to ISO 3394 carton plan dimensions; commission ISTA 3A testing on first production-representative packaged sample for both body material variants.

regulatory.name: Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (as amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory framework governing the classification, conformity assessment, and MHRA registration of medical devices placed on the Great Britain market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The Sentinel's fall-detection and emergency-call escalation pathway is a safety function that may cause the device to be classified as a medical device under UK MDR 2002. The report notes a launch strategy of Class I 'mobility aid with safety features' with an upgrade path to Class IIa once the emergency-call pathway is validated. Class I requires MHRA registration and a Declaration of Conformity; Class IIa requires a UK Approved Body audit.
regulatory.designImpact: Classification decision drives the entire quality management and technical file structure. If Class IIa is reached, the fall-detection algorithm must be validated as a medical software function under BS EN 62304 and risk-managed under BS EN ISO 14971. Class I still requires a technical file, labelling compliance, and post-market surveillance plan.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: MHRA device registration (Class I self-certification or Class IIa UK Approved Body certificate); Declaration of Conformity; technical file including intended purpose statement, classification justification, and post-market surveillance plan.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a UK regulatory affairs consultant to produce a formal classification opinion under UK MDR 2002 Rule 1 / Rule 10 before any other compliance work is scoped, as classification determines the entire regulatory pathway.

regulatory.name: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes
regulatory.summary: Quality management system standard required for medical device manufacturers; underpins UK MDR 2002 conformity assessment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Required if Sentinel is confirmed as a medical device under UK MDR 2002; the QMS must cover design, manufacture, and post-market surveillance of the device and its software.
regulatory.designImpact: Requires documented design controls, design history file, supplier qualification for battery and cellular module, and a post-market surveillance procedure. All design changes must go through a controlled change process.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN ISO 13485 certification from a UKAS-accredited certification body (if Class IIa); or documented QMS aligned to 13485 as part of the technical file (Class I). MHRA may inspect.
regulatory.gapAction: Determine classification first; then either implement a lite QMS for Class I or engage a certification body for full 13485 audit if Class IIa is required.

regulatory.name: Medical devices — Application of risk management to medical devices
regulatory.summary: Risk management process standard for medical devices; mandatory reference under UK MDR 2002 conformity assessment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies to the fall-detection classifier, the alert escalation pathway, and the physical mobility-aid function if the device is confirmed as a medical device. Risk management must cover both hardware failure modes (ferrule failure, battery failure) and software failure modes (missed fall, false positive causing unnecessary alarm).
regulatory.designImpact: Requires a risk management file with hazard identification, risk estimation, risk control measures, and residual risk evaluation for every foreseeable use and misuse scenario. The fall-detection classifier must have a defined sensitivity/specificity operating point justified by risk analysis.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk management file (hazard log, FMEA, risk control traceability matrix, residual risk acceptability statement) reviewed and approved by a competent person.
regulatory.gapAction: Begin hazard identification workshop covering physical, software, and connectivity failure modes; appoint a risk management file owner.

regulatory.name: Medical device software — Software life cycle processes
regulatory.summary: Software development and maintenance lifecycle standard for medical device software; required where software contributes to a safety function.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The fall-detection classifier and gait-analysis inference running on the nRF9160 and NPU co-processor are safety-related software functions. If the device is classified as a medical device, BS EN 62304 applies to all software contributing to the intended purpose, including firmware and the companion app alert pathway.
regulatory.designImpact: Software must be assigned a safety class (A, B, or C) based on the severity of harm from software failure. Fall detection missing a real fall is likely Class B or C, requiring documented software requirements, architecture, unit testing, and anomaly resolution.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Software development plan, software requirements specification, architecture document, unit and integration test records, anomaly log — all forming part of the technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Classify software safety class under BS EN 62304 clause 4.3 and establish a version-controlled software development environment with traceability from requirements to test.

regulatory.name: Radio Equipment Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/1206) — UK implementation of RED
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring radio equipment (including cellular devices) to meet essential requirements for safety, EMC, and efficient use of spectrum before being placed on the GB market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The nRF9160 LTE-M/NB-IoT cellular module and GPS receiver make Sentinel radio equipment under the Radio Equipment Regulations 2017. UKCA marking is required. Module-level certification from Nordic/the module supplier may carry through to system level if the antenna and RF environment are not materially changed — but the carbon-fibre shaft RF attenuation and the wood-handle antenna window must be assessed.
regulatory.designImpact: Antenna placement must be in the dielectric wood handle or a dielectric collar — not inside the carbon-fibre shaft — to preserve the module's certified RF performance. Any antenna modification or novel placement requires system-level radiated emissions and sensitivity testing. The charging stand's inductive link must also be assessed for spurious emissions.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing Radio Equipment Regulations 2017; module supplier's type-approval certificate (Ofcom/GSMA); system-level radiated emissions test report from a UKAS-accredited test house if antenna placement differs from module reference design.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain nRF9160 module supplier's regulatory certification pack; commission antenna placement review and, if required, system-level RF testing at a UKAS-accredited EMC lab.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring apparatus to not cause harmful interference and to have adequate immunity; applies to all electrical and electronic equipment placed on the GB market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel contains a cellular radio, IMU, NPU, and inductive charging link, all of which are potential emission sources. The device is also held by a person, making ESD immunity (EN 61000-4-2) particularly relevant given the capacitive grip sensor and conductive-adjacent handle surfaces.
regulatory.designImpact: PCB layout must minimise radiated emissions from the cellular module, NPU, and inductive charging link. ESD immunity testing at ±4 kV contact discharge is required for the handle. Conformal coating of the PCB is recommended. The charging stand must also be assessed for conducted and radiated emissions.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report (emissions and immunity) from a UKAS-accredited test house covering EN 55032 (emissions), EN 55035 (immunity), and EN 61000-4-2 (ESD); UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing EMC Regulations 2016.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage EMC test house early in PCB design phase for pre-compliance scanning; schedule formal EMC type-test once prototype is stable.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime implementing the Low Voltage Directive for electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC; the charging stand (mains-powered) falls within scope.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The inductive charging stand is mains-powered and must comply with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016. The Sentinel stick itself operates at low voltage from the internal battery and is not directly in scope, but the battery charging circuit and inductive receiver must be designed to safe isolation principles.
regulatory.designImpact: The charging stand must meet the safety requirements of BS EN 60335-1 (household appliances) and BS EN 60335-2-29 (battery chargers) as designated standards. Creepage and clearance distances, thermal cutoffs, and earth continuity (if Class I) or double insulation (Class II) must be designed in.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Type-test report for the charging stand against BS EN 60335-1 and BS EN 60335-2-29 from a UKAS-accredited test house; UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm charging stand safety class (Class I or II) and commission BS EN 60335-1/-2-29 type-testing for the stand as a separate product.

regulatory.name: Household and similar electrical appliances — Safety — Part 1: General requirements
regulatory.summary: Designated standard for household electrical appliance safety; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the mains-powered charging stand.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Serves the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the inductive charging stand. The stand is a mains-connected household appliance and must pass BS EN 60335-1 general requirements plus BS EN 60335-2-29 (battery chargers) as the particular standard.
regulatory.designImpact: Charging stand must pass dielectric strength, leakage current, thermal endurance, and abnormal operation tests. Inductive coupling efficiency and thermal behaviour under misalignment (stick not properly seated) must be characterised and shown to be safe.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN 60335-1 and BS EN 60335-2-29 type-test certificate from a UKAS-accredited test house.
regulatory.gapAction: Include charging stand in the test scope when engaging the safety test house; provide worst-case misalignment scenario for thermal testing.

regulatory.name: Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring consumer connectable products to meet minimum security requirements (no default passwords, vulnerability disclosure policy, minimum security update period stated).
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel is a consumer connectable product with cellular connectivity, a companion app, and cloud backend. The PSTI Act 2022 and the Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023 apply from April 2024. The eSIM and LTE-M link are in scope.
regulatory.designImpact: Firmware must not use universal default passwords. The founder must publish a vulnerability disclosure policy before launch. The stated minimum period for security updates must be declared in product documentation. The companion app and cloud API must be assessed for PSTI compliance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Statement of compliance with PSTI security requirements; published vulnerability disclosure policy URL; security update period declaration in product documentation; internal security assessment record.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a product security lead; draft vulnerability disclosure policy and security update commitment; conduct threat modelling of the cellular link, eSIM, and companion app API.

regulatory.name: UK General Data Protection Regulation and Data Protection Act 2018
regulatory.summary: UK statutory data protection framework governing collection, processing, and storage of personal data including health and location data.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel continuously collects GPS location, gait patterns, fall events, and voice audio — all of which are personal data, and gait/health data is special category data under UK GDPR Article 9. The companion app and alarm receiving centre data flows must be mapped and lawful bases established. Data residency (UK vs. overseas cloud) must be addressed.
regulatory.designImpact: Privacy by design must be embedded: data minimisation on-device (process gait locally, transmit only events), explicit consent or legitimate interest basis for health data, data retention limits, and right-to-erasure capability in the companion app and backend. The microphone must only activate on defined triggers, not continuously stream.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) for the health and location data processing; ICO registration (if not already held); privacy notice; data processing agreements with alarm receiving centre and cloud provider; records of processing activities.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a DPIA covering GPS, gait, fall-event, and audio data flows; engage a data protection solicitor to review the companion app privacy notice and alarm-centre data processing agreement.

regulatory.name: Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime governing electronic communications, cookies, and direct marketing; relevant to the companion app and any SMS/voice alert communications.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The fall-alert SMS and voice calls to family members, and any push notifications from the companion app, are electronic communications subject to PECR. Consent and opt-out mechanisms must be designed into the alert configuration flow.
regulatory.designImpact: Alert recipients (family members) must have given valid consent to receive automated SMS and voice calls from the Sentinel system. The companion app must not use tracking cookies or analytics without consent. The alert escalation flow must include an opt-out or preference management mechanism.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Legal review of alert consent mechanism; companion app cookie/tracking consent implementation; records of consent for alert recipients.
regulatory.gapAction: Include PECR consent flow in companion app UX design; obtain legal review of the automated SMS/voice alert consent mechanism before launch.

regulatory.name: Ofcom Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 — General Authorisation for LTE-M/NB-IoT spectrum use
regulatory.summary: UK spectrum authorisation framework; LTE-M and NB-IoT operate in licensed spectrum held by MNOs, so the device itself does not require a separate Ofcom licence but must use a certified module.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The nRF9160 LTE-M/NB-IoT radio operates in licensed spectrum. Ofcom compliance is achieved via the module supplier's type approval. The eSIM (MFF2 form factor) must comply with GSMA SGP.02 (M2M eSIM specification) for remote SIM provisioning. The founder must have an MVNO or MNO agreement for the eSIM profile.
regulatory.designImpact: The nRF9160 module must carry valid Ofcom/ETSI type approval. The eSIM provisioning platform must support remote profile management for the lifetime of the product (minimum security update period declared under PSTI). Roaming behaviour must be tested for UK network coverage edge cases.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: nRF9160 module type-approval certificate (ETSI/Ofcom); MVNO/MNO eSIM service agreement; GSMA SGP.02 compliance confirmation from eSIM platform provider.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm nRF9160 module type-approval status with Nordic or module supplier; engage an MVNO (e.g. Eseye, Transatel) for eSIM provisioning and obtain SGP.02 compliance documentation.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime restricting hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, and four phthalates) in electrical and electronic equipment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel and its charging stand are electrical and electronic equipment placed on the GB market and must comply with RoHS 2012. The PCB, solder, battery, and cable assemblies must use compliant materials. Supplier declarations are required for all in-scope components.
regulatory.designImpact: PCB must use lead-free solder (SAC alloy). All components must have RoHS-compliant material declarations. The battery cell chemistry must be confirmed as RoHS-compliant. The wood handle finish (lacquer or oil) must be assessed for restricted substances.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity; supplier RoHS material declarations for all electronic components; technical documentation file.
regulatory.gapAction: Include RoHS compliance requirements in component procurement specifications; obtain supplier declarations for all electronic components and battery cells.

regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring producers of electrical and electronic equipment to fund collection, treatment, and recycling of waste EEE.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel and its charging stand are EEE placed on the GB market. The founder must register as a producer with a UK WEEE compliance scheme before first sale and meet annual reporting obligations. The WEEE symbol must appear on the product and packaging.
regulatory.designImpact: Product labelling must include the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol. The battery must be designed to be removable for separate recycling (or a take-back scheme must be established). Packaging must include WEEE disposal instructions.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration certificate from a UK compliance scheme (e.g. Valpak, Clarity); annual WEEE return records.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK WEEE compliance scheme before first product sale; add WEEE symbol to product and packaging artwork.
