regulatory.name: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/2164) as amended
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime governing the placing on the market of batteries and accumulators, including labelling, collection, and recycling obligations for portable batteries.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The lithium-ion battery pack inside Sentinel is a portable battery placed on the GB market as part of the product. The founder must register as a battery producer and meet collection/recycling targets. The battery must be labelled with the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol and the chemical symbol for lithium (Li).
regulatory.designImpact: Battery must be labelled. If the battery is not user-removable (embedded in the shaft cavity), the founder must provide a take-back or end-of-life return mechanism. Battery capacity and chemistry must be declared.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Battery producer registration with a UK compliance scheme; battery labelling compliance; annual battery producer return.
regulatory.gapAction: Register as a battery producer with a UK compliance scheme; confirm battery labelling requirements with the scheme administrator; design end-of-life battery return process.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium metal and lithium ion batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety tests for lithium cells and batteries required before shipping by road, sea, or air.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The lithium-ion battery pack (whether 18650 or custom cylindrical cell) must have UN 38.3 certification before it can be transported. This applies to inbound shipment of cells from the supplier and to outbound shipment of finished Sentinel units. The Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs) and IATA DGR apply.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery pack design (cell + PCM/BMS) must be tested as a unit to UN 38.3 (altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, external short, impact, overcharge, forced discharge). The BMS must prevent overcharge and over-discharge. Packaging for shipping must meet IATA PI 967 (equipment containing batteries).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell/pack supplier or accredited test lab; ADR/CDG dangerous goods note for road transport of cells; IATA DGR compliant shipping documentation for air freight.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm cell supplier has a valid UN 38.3 test report for the chosen cell; if a custom pack is designed, commission UN 38.3 testing before first shipment.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for portable sealed lithium secondary cells, and for batteries made from them, for use in portable applications — Part 2: Lithium systems
regulatory.summary: Safety standard for lithium-ion battery packs used in portable consumer applications; designated standard for battery safety under the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Serves the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the Sentinel lithium-ion battery pack. The pack (cell + BMS/PCM) must be tested to BS EN IEC 62133-2 for overcharge, over-discharge, short circuit, crush, and thermal abuse. The report explicitly references IEC 62133 as required.
regulatory.designImpact: BMS must include over-charge, over-discharge, short-circuit, and thermal protection. The pack must pass cell-level and pack-level abuse tests. The inductive charging circuit must not be capable of overcharging the pack under any fault condition.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 62133-2 type-test certificate for the battery pack from a UKAS-accredited test house; supplier declaration if using a pre-certified pack.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain BS EN IEC 62133-2 test report from battery pack supplier; if designing a custom pack, commission testing at a UKAS-accredited lab.

regulatory.name: Assistive products for walking — Requirements and test methods — Part 1: Elbow crutches
regulatory.summary: Structural and performance standard for walking aids; the closest applicable standard for walking sticks in the UK market, covering static load, fatigue, and stability testing.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Serves the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 and the General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (GPSR) for the physical walking-stick function. The report explicitly identifies BS EN ISO 11334-1 as the governing standard for UK market mobility-aid loads. The carbon-fibre shaft, telescoping joint, and ferrule must all be designed and tested to the load cases in this standard (static load ≥ 1000 N, fatigue cycling).
regulatory.designImpact: The carbon-fibre shaft wall thickness (1.0–1.5 mm) and telescoping collar must be validated by structural test to BS EN ISO 11334-1 load cases. The tungsten/rubber ferrule must meet slip-resistance requirements. The electronics cavity must not compromise shaft structural integrity — FEA and physical testing required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN ISO 11334-1 type-test report from an accredited test house covering static strength, fatigue, and stability; FEA report for the modified shaft with electronics cavity.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission FEA of the carbon-fibre shaft with the electronics cavity cut-out; engage a test house to conduct BS EN ISO 11334-1 structural and fatigue testing on prototype shafts.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the GB market; may apply to the telescoping adjustment mechanism and any motorised or spring-loaded components.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The telescoping length-adjustment mechanism (twist-lock or push-button collar) is a mechanical assembly with a defined adjustment function. If the collar uses a spring-loaded detent, the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 may apply. Even if the device is considered a simple tool rather than machinery, the essential health and safety requirements inform the design of the adjustment mechanism and handle-shaft interface.
regulatory.designImpact: The telescoping collar must not release unexpectedly under load. The adjustment mechanism must be operable by an older adult with reduced grip strength and dexterity. A risk assessment under BS EN ISO 12100 is required for the mechanical assembly.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk assessment under BS EN ISO 12100 for the telescoping mechanism; mechanical test evidence that the collar does not release under the BS EN ISO 11334-1 load cases.
regulatory.gapAction: Conduct a BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment for the telescoping mechanism; include collar release force and accidental-release testing in the BS EN ISO 11334-1 test programme.

regulatory.name: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (SI 2005/1803) — to be superseded by GPSR 2024
regulatory.summary: UK statutory baseline safety requirement for all consumer products not covered by a specific product safety directive; requires products to be safe and producers to monitor and act on safety issues.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel is a consumer product sold to members of the public. The General Product Safety Regulations 2005 apply as a baseline. Note: the UK is implementing the updated General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) which will replace the 2005 Regulations; the founder should monitor the implementation timeline and ensure compliance with the updated regime.
regulatory.designImpact: The product must be safe for its intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse by older adults, including those with reduced cognitive function. A post-market surveillance plan and product recall procedure must be in place before launch.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Post-market surveillance plan; product recall procedure; consumer safety assessment documented in the technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Draft a post-market surveillance plan and product recall procedure; monitor UK GPSR 2024 implementation timeline and update compliance documentation accordingly.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) marking obligations under the Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019
regulatory.summary: UK statutory umbrella marking scheme required for products placed on the Great Britain market that previously required CE marking; covers electrical safety, EMC, radio equipment, and medical devices.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sentinel and its charging stand require UKCA marking before being placed on the GB market. The marking must be affixed to the product (or packaging if the product is too small) and accompanied by a UK Declaration of Conformity referencing all applicable regulations (Radio Equipment Regulations 2017, EMC Regulations 2016, Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, and UK MDR 2002 if classified as a medical device).
regulatory.designImpact: The UKCA mark and UK Declaration of Conformity must be prepared before first sale. The technical file must be held by a UK Responsible Person. If the manufacturer is outside the UK, a UK Responsible Person must be appointed. The mark must not be affixed until all conformity assessments are complete.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UK Declaration of Conformity covering all applicable regulations; technical file held by UK Responsible Person; UKCA mark on product or packaging.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK Responsible Person (if manufacturer is outside UK); prepare a UKCA marking plan listing all applicable regulations and the conformity assessment route for each.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (SI 1989/635)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime imposing duties on employers and employees to prevent danger from electrical systems in the workplace; relevant to the design and testing of the electrical system within Sentinel and its charging stand.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The internal electrical system of Sentinel (battery, BMS, cellular module, inductive charging receiver) and the charging stand (mains-connected) must be designed so that they do not create electrical danger. EAWR applies to the design and manufacturing environment and to any workplace installation of the charging stand (e.g. in a care home).
regulatory.designImpact: The BMS must prevent dangerous overcharge, over-discharge, and short-circuit conditions. The inductive charging link must be designed so that a fault in the stand cannot cause a dangerous condition in the stick. Isolation between the mains supply and the low-voltage electronics must be demonstrated.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical safety test records (dielectric strength, insulation resistance, leakage current) for the charging stand; BMS protection function test records.
regulatory.gapAction: Include EAWR-relevant electrical safety tests in the charging stand type-test programme; document BMS protection function verification in the technical file.

regulatory.name: Photobiological safety of lamps and lamp systems
regulatory.summary: Standard assessing photobiological hazard of optical radiation sources; relevant if the charging stand or device uses LEDs for status indication.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — If the charging stand or Sentinel handle uses LEDs for charging status or alert indication, BS EN 62471 applies to assess photobiological risk. Older adults may have reduced ability to avoid prolonged exposure to bright LEDs. Serves the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: Any status LEDs must be assessed for photobiological hazard class. LEDs visible to the user should be Exempt or Risk Group 1 at worst. LED drive current and viewing angle must be controlled.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Photobiological safety assessment (manufacturer's calculation or test report) for any LEDs used in the product or charging stand.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify all LEDs in the design; obtain photobiological safety data from LED supplier and confirm Exempt or RG1 classification; document in technical file.

regulatory.code: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (ESQCR)
regulatory.name: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002
regulatory.summary: Statutory instrument governing the safety, quality, and continuity of electricity supply and distribution networks in Great Britain; applies to any equipment connected to the public network.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — AC grid connection point of the BESS; ESQCR imposes duties on the network operator and on the producer/consumer connecting generation or storage in parallel with the distribution network. G99 sits under ESQCR as the DNO-enforced engineering recommendation.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must meet voltage, frequency, power factor, and harmonic limits set by ESQCR and enforced via G99; protection relay settings must be agreed with the host DNO before energisation.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: DNO connection agreement referencing ESQCR compliance; G99 commissioning test record signed by DNO witness; protection relay settings schedule accepted by DNO.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage host DNO to open a G99 connection application and obtain draft connection agreement referencing ESQCR obligations.

regulatory.name: Requirements for the Connection of Generation Equipment in Parallel with Public Distribution Networks above 16 A per Phase
regulatory.summary: ENA Engineering Recommendation mandating protection, control, and commissioning requirements for storage and generation connecting to UK distribution networks above 16 A per phase.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Behind-the-meter grid connection at >16 A per phase; G99 is the DNO-enforced engineering recommendation sitting under ESQCR. Grid-forming capability and islanding detection are explicitly required for this system.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must support grid-forming mode, loss-of-mains (LoM) protection (ROCOF and vector shift), frequency and voltage ride-through, and reactive power capability; protection settings must be pre-loaded and witnessed by the DNO at commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: G99 application acceptance from host DNO; commissioning test record including LoM, ROCOF, and ride-through tests signed by DNO witness; generation connection agreement.
regulatory.gapAction: Submit G99 application to host DNO at earliest opportunity; confirm DNO witness availability within the two-day commissioning window and pre-load protection settings before site arrival.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1101)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Low Voltage Directive for electrical equipment operating between 50 V and 1,000 V AC or 75 V and 1,500 V DC; requires UKCA marking and a declaration of conformity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Complete BESS electrical assembly including PCS, BMS, auxiliary LV distribution, and UPS operating within LV range; UKCA marking is mandatory for placing on the UK market. Demonstrated via harmonised designated standards BS EN IEC 62933-5-2, BS EN IEC 62619, and BS EN IEC 63056.
regulatory.designImpact: System-level design must achieve the essential safety requirements of the Regulations; requires documented risk assessment, technical file, and conformity assessment before the unit is placed on the UK market or put into service.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing applicable harmonised standards; technical construction file held by the responsible person; UKCA mark affixed to the container nameplate.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify the UK responsible person (manufacturer or importer); commission technical file compilation and draft Declaration of Conformity aligned to BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 and BS EN IEC 62619.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to be designed so that electromagnetic disturbance generated does not exceed levels that prevent other equipment from operating normally, and that the apparatus has adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — PCS inverter, BMS electronics, SCADA gateway, and auxiliary controls; high-power bi-directional inverters are significant sources of conducted and radiated EMC emissions and must not disturb adjacent equipment or the distribution network.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must meet harmonic emission limits (G99 / BS EN 61000-3-12 for >16 A equipment) and immunity requirements; shielding, filtering, and cable segregation strategy required in the electrical room design.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report from a UKAS-accredited laboratory or competent body demonstrating compliance with relevant BS EN 61000 series limits; UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing EMC Regulations 2016.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify EMC emission and immunity requirements in PCS procurement; obtain EMC test reports from PCS supplier and verify they cover the installed configuration.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989
regulatory.summary: Statutory instrument imposing duties on employers and employees to prevent danger from electrical systems in the workplace; applies to all electrical systems at work premises.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical systems within the container and at the site connection point during installation, commissioning, operation, and maintenance; imposes duty on the site operator and the commissioning team.
regulatory.designImpact: Electrical systems must be constructed and maintained to prevent danger; requires safe isolation procedures, written schemes of examination, and competent persons for all live-working or testing activities during commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written scheme of examination for the BESS electrical system; safe isolation and lock-off procedures documented in the O&M manual; records of competent-person inspections.
regulatory.gapAction: Draft written scheme of examination and safe isolation procedures for inclusion in the O&M manual; confirm commissioning team competency records are available before site mobilisation.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations governing the design, installation, inspection, and testing of fixed low-voltage electrical installations; de facto enforcement standard for EAWR in fixed installations.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal LV wiring, protection coordination, earthing, and isolation within the container; demonstrates compliance with EAWR and the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the fixed installation. Applies from the container's incoming terminals to all internal circuits.
regulatory.designImpact: Internal distribution must comply with shock protection (ADS), earthing system selection (TN-S or TT depending on site supply), overcurrent and fault protection, RCD protection on auxiliary circuits, and cable sizing for continuous 1.5 MW DC and AC currents in a thermally challenging environment.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) signed by a qualified and competent person; Schedule of Inspections and Schedule of Test Results; periodic inspection regime documented in O&M manual.
regulatory.gapAction: Design internal distribution to BS 7671 18th Edition including earthing strategy and protection coordination; engage a qualified electrician to produce the EIC after factory integration and before shipment.

regulatory.name: Electrical Energy Storage (EES) Systems — Part 5-2: Safety Requirements for Grid-Integrated Electrical Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: Harmonised designated standard specifying safety requirements for stationary grid-integrated EES systems; the primary system-level safety standard for UK BESS UKCA compliance.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Complete containerised BESS system including battery racks, PCS, BMS, thermal management, and fire system; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 under the UKCA scheme. Covers thermal runaway propagation, fire containment, ventilation, and protection coordination at system level.
regulatory.designImpact: System must pass or demonstrate compliance with fire propagation tests, thermal runaway containment requirements, ventilation and gas detection provisions, and protection coordination; dictates integration of certified fire detection and suppression, deflagration venting, and off-gas management.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: System-level test report from a UKAS-accredited laboratory or recognised third-party certification body demonstrating compliance with BS EN IEC 62933-5-2; or supplier-held type-test certificate covering this system configuration.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm with the chosen integrator (e.g. Sungrow, BYD, CATL) whether their containerised product holds a current BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 type-test certificate; if not, scope a system-level test programme with a UKAS-accredited test house.

regulatory.name: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes — Safety Requirements for Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries for Use in Industrial Applications
regulatory.summary: Harmonised designated standard specifying safety requirements for lithium cells and batteries used in industrial applications including stationary energy storage.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LFP cell modules and battery racks within the BESS; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at cell and module level. Required by the report as the cell-level safety standard.
regulatory.designImpact: Cells and modules must pass abuse tests (overcharge, over-discharge, short circuit, thermal abuse, mechanical abuse); BMS must implement the protection functions specified in the standard; supplier must hold valid certification.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Cell and module supplier's BS EN IEC 62619 type-test certificate from an accredited laboratory; BMS protection function verification records.
regulatory.gapAction: Request BS EN IEC 62619 certification documentation from the LFP cell and module supplier during procurement; verify certificate scope covers the specific cell format and module configuration selected.

regulatory.name: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes — Safety Requirements for Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries for Use in Electrical Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: Harmonised designated standard extending lithium battery safety requirements specifically to stationary electrical energy storage system applications, complementing BS EN IEC 62619.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Battery system (racks integrated with BMS and thermal management) as a complete energy storage assembly; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at battery-system level, bridging cell certification (BS EN IEC 62619) and system certification (BS EN IEC 62933-5-2).
regulatory.designImpact: Battery system must demonstrate safe behaviour under system-level fault conditions including thermal runaway propagation between modules; rack design, inter-module spacing, and BMS fault response must satisfy the standard's requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Battery system supplier's BS EN IEC 63056 type-test certificate or test report; confirmation that the certificate covers the rack configuration and module count used in this 3.5 MWh system.
regulatory.gapAction: Request BS EN IEC 63056 system-level certification from the battery rack supplier; confirm the certificate scope matches the rack count and configuration in the chosen integrator's design.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the UK market; applies to machinery with moving parts presenting hazards.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Liquid cooling skid (pumps, fans, compressors), automated fire suppression actuators, and any motorised ventilation or isolation systems within the container; these constitute machinery with moving parts and control systems presenting mechanical and electrical hazards.
regulatory.designImpact: Cooling skid and ventilation machinery must meet essential health and safety requirements; requires risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100, guarding of moving parts, emergency stop provision, and CE/UKCA marking on the machinery sub-assembly.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the cooling skid and any motorised sub-assemblies; technical file including risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100; UKCA mark on the machinery nameplate.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm with the cooling skid supplier that their equipment holds UKCA (or CE transitional) marking under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008; obtain Declaration of Conformity and technical file summary.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (HSWA)
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety legislation imposing general duties on employers, designers, manufacturers, and suppliers to ensure safety of persons at work and affected by work activities.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Design, manufacture, installation, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the BESS; Section 6 imposes duties on the designer and manufacturer to ensure the system is safe and without risks to health when properly used; Section 2 imposes duties on the site operator as employer.
regulatory.designImpact: Requires documented hazard identification and risk assessment covering electrical, fire, chemical (electrolyte, glycol coolant, suppression agent), and mechanical hazards; safe systems of work must be documented in the O&M manual for all foreseeable maintenance tasks.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Design risk assessment (HAZID/HAZOP or equivalent); O&M manual with safe systems of work; COSHH assessments for glycol coolant and fire suppression agent; site-specific risk assessment for installation and commissioning.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a HAZID/HAZOP for the integrated system design; prepare COSHH assessments for coolant and suppression agent; include safe systems of work in the O&M manual before first shipment.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on clients, designers, and contractors for health and safety in construction projects; applies to installation of the BESS on a prepared site.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Site installation phase including concrete pad preparation, container placement, anchorage, AC tie-in, and commissioning; CDM applies to any construction work including installation of fixed plant on a prepared foundation. The client (site owner) and the principal designer/contractor have statutory duties.
regulatory.designImpact: Pre-construction information must be provided to the installation team; a construction phase plan must be prepared; health and safety file must be handed over to the site owner on completion. Container design must consider safe installation sequences (lifting, anchorage, cable entry).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Pre-construction information pack; construction phase plan prepared by principal contractor; health and safety file handed to client on completion of installation.
regulatory.gapAction: Advise the site client of their CDM duties as client; prepare pre-construction information pack covering the BESS installation scope; confirm whether a principal designer appointment is required based on project scale.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium Metal and Lithium Ion Batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory international transport safety test protocol for lithium cells and batteries; required before any lithium battery shipment by road, sea, or air.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LFP cell modules and battery racks during transport from manufacturer to UK site; UN 38.3 is mandated by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs) for road transport and by IMDG Code for sea freight.
regulatory.designImpact: All LFP cells and battery modules must have passed UN 38.3 altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, external short circuit, impact/crush, overcharge, and forced discharge tests before shipment; this constrains cell and module selection to certified products.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from the cell and module supplier or an accredited laboratory; dangerous goods note (DGN) for road transport under CDG Regs; IMDG declaration for sea freight if applicable.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm during cell and module procurement that the supplier holds a current UN 38.3 test summary report covering the specific cell format; obtain the report and prepare CDG dangerous goods documentation for UK road transport legs.

regulatory.code: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs / ADR)
regulatory.name: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing ADR for road transport of dangerous goods including lithium batteries (UN 3480 / UN 3481); applies to transport of battery modules to site.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Road transport of LFP battery modules and racks from port or warehouse to installation site on UK roads; lithium ion batteries are classified as Class 9 dangerous goods under ADR and require compliant packaging, marking, documentation, and driver training.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery modules must be transported in ADR-compliant packaging or as installed equipment in the container (if transported as a complete unit, different provisions apply); transport plan must address quantity thresholds and exemption limits.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: ADR dangerous goods note; driver Vocational Training Certificate (ADR certificate) if above exemption thresholds; packaging compliance records; transport emergency card (TREM card).
regulatory.gapAction: Determine whether battery modules are transported separately or as part of the complete integrated container; prepare ADR documentation accordingly and confirm haulier holds appropriate ADR certification.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Specification and Testing — Part 1: General Cargo Containers for General Purposes
regulatory.summary: International standard specifying structural requirements and test methods for ISO Series 1 freight containers; the basis for the CSC plate certification.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — 40-foot High Cube container shell used as the BESS enclosure; the original CSC plate and ISO 1496-1 structural certification are voided once the container shell is structurally modified by cutting vents, deflagration panels, large cable gland openings, roof penetrations for the cooling skid, or internal bracing for battery rack loads. Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is then required.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate is voided by structural modifications (vent openings, roof penetrations, internal rack bracing); design must rely on alternative structural certification — finite element analysis to BS EN 1993 (Eurocode 3) or new inspection by a recognised classification society — to demonstrate structural adequacy for transport and installed loads.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Finite element analysis report demonstrating structural adequacy of the modified container under transport and installed load cases; or new structural certificate from a recognised classification society (e.g. Lloyd's Register, DNV); updated load rating documentation for transport.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission structural analysis of the modified container design (including all penetrations and internal bracing) against transport and installed load cases; engage a classification society or structural engineer to certify the modified structure before first shipment.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Corner Fittings — Specification
regulatory.summary: International standard specifying the geometry and strength of ISO corner castings used for lifting, stacking, and securing freight containers.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Eight ISO 1161 corner castings on the 40-foot High Cube container used for four-point crane lifting during site placement and for foundation anchorage via M24/M30 bolts; corner castings must be undamaged and correctly loaded during lifting operations.
regulatory.designImpact: Lifting plan must use a four-point spreader bar matched to the 12,192 mm × 2,438 mm corner casting pattern; crane and HIAB rated for up to 40 t; foundation anchor bolt design must account for point loads up to approximately 10 t per corner under seismic and wind load cases.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Lifting plan prepared by a competent lifting engineer; crane/HIAB rated capacity certificate; foundation anchor bolt design calculation signed by a structural engineer; site-specific risk assessment for lifting operation.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a lifting plan referencing ISO 1161 corner casting loads for the maximum system weight; commission foundation anchor bolt design from a structural engineer before concrete pad construction.

regulatory.name: Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems (2023 Edition)
regulatory.summary: US reference standard for stationary ESS installation; widely cited by UK insurers, NFCC, and planning authorities as a design reference for fire safety and separation distances.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Fire safety design, separation distances, suppression system sizing, and deflagration vent area calculation; not UK statute but cited in NFCC Grid Scale BESS Operational Guidance and likely required by commercial insurers and planning authorities. UK statutory peer for system-level fire safety is BS EN IEC 62933-5-2.
regulatory.designImpact: Separation distances (minimum 3 m from property lines and occupied buildings), deflagration vent area calculation, suppression system density, smoke and gas detection zoning, and emergency services access route must be designed to NFPA 855 principles to satisfy NFCC guidance and insurer requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Fire safety design report referencing NFPA 855 separation distances and suppression sizing; deflagration vent area calculation; insurer alignment statement confirming NFPA 855 design basis accepted.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a fire safety design report referencing NFPA 855 and NFCC Grid Scale BESS guidance; include separation distance calculations and deflagration vent sizing; submit to commercial insurer for underwriting review.

regulatory.name: Standard for Energy Storage Systems and Equipment
regulatory.summary: US certification standard for complete energy storage systems; referenced by NFCC guidance and UK insurers as evidence of system-level safety testing.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Complete BESS system; not UK statute but the report explicitly recommends UL 9540 listing for NFCC alignment. UK statutory peer is BS EN IEC 62933-5-2. Insurers and planning authorities may require evidence of UL 9540 listing or equivalent in the absence of a BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 type-test certificate.
regulatory.designImpact: If the chosen integrator holds UL 9540 listing, this provides supporting evidence for the fire safety case; the listing scope must cover the specific container configuration including fire suppression type and battery chemistry.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UL 9540 listing certificate from the integrator covering the specific system configuration; or equivalent BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 type-test certificate accepted by the insurer as a substitute.
regulatory.gapAction: During integrator selection, confirm whether the product holds UL 9540 listing and/or BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 type-test certification; obtain certificate scope documents and assess coverage against the project configuration.

regulatory.name: Test Method for Evaluating Thermal Runaway Fire Propagation in Battery Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: US test method for evaluating thermal runaway propagation at cell, module, unit, and installation levels; referenced by NFCC and insurers to demonstrate fire containment.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Thermal runaway propagation behaviour of the LFP battery rack configuration; not UK statute but cited in NFCC Grid Scale BESS Operational Guidance and required by many UK commercial insurers as evidence that thermal runaway does not propagate between modules or to adjacent units.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery rack spacing, inter-module barriers, BMS fault response speed, and suppression system activation timing must be designed to prevent propagation; UL 9540A test results at module and unit level inform the fire safety case submitted to the insurer and planning authority.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UL 9540A test report at module level and unit level from the battery rack supplier or integrator; fire safety case referencing UL 9540A results submitted to insurer and planning authority.
regulatory.gapAction: Request UL 9540A test reports from the battery rack supplier covering the specific module format and rack configuration; if not available, scope a UL 9540A test programme as part of the system qualification plan.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safe design, installation, operation, and maintenance of pressure systems containing relevant fluids; applies to the liquid cooling circuit if operating above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Liquid cooling circuit (glycol/water loop) connecting the chiller skid to battery racks; if the system operates above 0.5 bar gauge with a pressure-volume product above the PSSR threshold, a written scheme of examination is required and periodic inspection by a competent person is mandatory.
regulatory.designImpact: Cooling circuit design must include pressure relief, safe isolation, and drainage provisions; a written scheme of examination must be prepared before the system is first operated; inspection intervals must be documented in the O&M manual.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written scheme of examination for the cooling pressure system prepared by a competent person; initial inspection certificate; periodic inspection records included in the O&M manual.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm operating pressure and pressure-volume product of the cooling circuit; if above PSSR thresholds, engage a competent person (e.g. insurer's engineer) to prepare the written scheme of examination before commissioning.

regulatory.code: Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002 (DSEAR)
regulatory.name: Dangerous Substances and Explosive Atmospheres Regulations 2002
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring employers to control risks from fire, explosion, and similar events arising from dangerous substances in the workplace; applies where flammable gases or vapours may be present.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Internal atmosphere of the BESS container where LFP cell off-gassing (hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and other flammable gases) during thermal runaway or overcharge events may create a flammable or explosive atmosphere; DSEAR requires hazardous area classification and appropriate equipment selection.
regulatory.designImpact: Hazardous area classification (Zone 0/1/2) must be assessed for the container interior; electrical equipment inside the container (sensors, BMS boards, lighting) must be selected to the appropriate Ex category if a hazardous zone is identified; ventilation design must prevent accumulation of flammable gases above 25% LEL.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: DSEAR risk assessment and hazardous area classification drawing; equipment selection schedule confirming Ex-rated equipment where required; ventilation calculation demonstrating gas concentration remains below 25% LEL under worst-case off-gas scenario.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a DSEAR hazardous area classification assessment for the container interior based on the LFP off-gas characterisation data; use results to specify appropriate electrical equipment categories for internal components.

regulatory.name: Waste Batteries and Accumulators Regulations 2009
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Batteries Directive; requires producers of batteries placed on the UK market to register, finance collection, and meet recycling targets.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LFP battery modules placed on the UK market as part of the BESS; the producer (manufacturer or importer) must register with an approved battery compliance scheme and finance end-of-life collection and recycling of the industrial batteries.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery modules must be designed for safe removal and recycling at end of life; the O&M manual must include end-of-life disposal instructions; the responsible person must be registered with a UK battery compliance scheme before placing the product on the market.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Registration certificate with a UK-approved battery compliance scheme (e.g. Valpak, Ecosurety); end-of-life disposal instructions in the O&M manual; battery labelling compliant with the Regulations.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK-approved battery compliance scheme before the first unit is placed on the UK market; confirm battery module labelling meets the Regulations' requirements.

regulatory.code: UKCA Marking (Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019)
regulatory.name: UKCA Marking Obligations — UK Conformity Assessed
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK market access scheme requiring UKCA marking on products placed on the Great Britain market that previously required CE marking; applies to electrical equipment, machinery, and EMC-regulated products.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Complete BESS unit placed on the Great Britain market; UKCA marking is required under the Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 as the umbrella conformity marking covering the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016, and Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
regulatory.designImpact: A single UKCA mark on the container nameplate covers all applicable regulations; requires a UK-based responsible person, a technical file for each applicable regulation, and a Declaration of Conformity referencing each applicable designated standard.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity signed by the UK responsible person; technical file held in the UK; UKCA mark affixed to the container nameplate in a visible and legible position.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK responsible person; compile the UKCA technical file covering all applicable regulations; draft and sign the Declaration of Conformity before the first unit is placed on the market.

regulatory.name: Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/614) — England
regulatory.summary: Statutory drinking-water quality standards for water supplied to consumers in England; sets parametric values for TDS, microbiological, chemical, and disinfection by-product limits.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Permeate water quality at point of supply; any water supplied to consumers or a distribution network must meet parametric values under Regulation 4. Applies directly when the unit supplies a municipal or relief network.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment train (remineralisation, chlorination) must be sized and validated to achieve <500 mg/L TDS, residual free chlorine 0.2–0.5 mg/L, and all Schedule 1 parametric values. Sampling ports and continuous monitoring instrumentation must be integrated.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test reports from an accredited laboratory demonstrating compliance with Schedule 1 parametric values; Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) acceptance or local authority notification where supply enters a public network.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission accredited laboratory water-quality testing programme against Schedule 1 parameters and establish DWI notification procedure for each deployment jurisdiction.

regulatory.name: BS 6920: Suitability of Non-Metallic Products for Use in Contact with Water Intended for Human Consumption
regulatory.summary: UK standard specifying tests for non-metallic materials and products in contact with potable water to ensure they do not impart taste, odour, or toxic substances.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — All non-metallic potable-contact components (UPVC/HDPE LP piping, FRP remineralisation vessel, permeate outlet flange lining, dosing tubing, seals, gaskets); demonstrates compliance with Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 and supports WRAS approval.
regulatory.designImpact: Every non-metallic component in the permeate flow path must be sourced with BS 6920 test evidence or WRAS approval. FRP remineralisation vessel, UPVC/HDPE piping, and all elastomeric seals on the permeate side must be individually assessed or carry WRAS listing.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS 6920 test certificates or WRAS Product Approval certificates for each non-metallic potable-contact component; supplier declarations referencing test reports.
regulatory.gapAction: Audit every non-metallic component in the permeate flow path against the WRAS approved-products list and obtain BS 6920 certificates for any unlisted items before procurement is finalised.

regulatory.name: WRAS Water Fittings Regulations Approval — Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999
regulatory.summary: UK approval scheme confirming that water fittings and materials do not contaminate, waste, or misuse water supplied by a water undertaker; underpins compliance with the Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All fittings, valves, and pipework on the potable (permeate) side of the unit that connect or could connect to a public water supply; Water Supply (Water Fittings) Regulations 1999 Regulation 4 prohibits use of non-approved fittings.
regulatory.designImpact: Permeate-side valves, connectors, flexible hoses, and the potable outlet flange assembly must carry WRAS approval or be individually tested. Backflow prevention device at the permeate outlet must meet Fluid Category 5 requirements given seawater feed risk.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WRAS approval certificates for all permeate-side fittings; backflow prevention device type-test certificate to BS EN 1717 at Fluid Category 5.
regulatory.gapAction: Cross-reference full permeate-side bill of materials against WRAS approved-products database and specify WRAS-listed backflow prevention at the permeate outlet.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000 (SI 2000/128)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime governing the safe design, installation, operation, and maintenance of pressure systems containing relevant fluids above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — HP piping loop (55–70 bar operating pressure), RO pressure vessels (rated 69–83 bar), ERD pressure exchanger, and high-pressure pump casing; all constitute a 'pressure system' under PSSR 2000 once installed and operated in the UK.
regulatory.designImpact: A Written Scheme of Examination (WSE) must be prepared by a competent person before first operation. HP pressure vessels and piping must be designed to PED/UKCA pressure equipment requirements with 1.5× safety factor. Periodic statutory inspection intervals must be defined in the WSE.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written Scheme of Examination prepared and certified by a competent person (typically a UK-registered inspection body such as Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas, or TÜV); inspection records at each deployment.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a UK-recognised inspection body to draft the Written Scheme of Examination covering HP vessels, piping, and ERD; incorporate inspection access points into the mechanical design.

regulatory.name: Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1105)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime for the design and manufacture of pressure equipment and assemblies placed on the UK market; implements UKCA marking obligations for pressure equipment above threshold PS×V limits.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Manufacture and first placing on market of the HP pressure vessels (69–83 bar FRP), HP pump casing, ERD, and the assembled pressure system as a 'pressure equipment assembly'; PESR 2016 applies at manufacture stage, PSSR 2000 applies in service.
regulatory.designImpact: HP FRP RO pressure vessels and the assembled HP loop must be classified under PESR 2016 categories (likely Category III or IV given pressure×volume product); conformity assessment by a UK Approved Body required before UKCA marking. Design documentation, material traceability, and hydrostatic test records required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for each pressure vessel and the HP assembly; UK Approved Body (e.g. Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas) conformity assessment certificate; hydrostatic test records at 1.5× MAWP.
regulatory.gapAction: Classify each HP component under PESR 2016 Schedule 2 categories, identify a UK Approved Body, and initiate conformity assessment in parallel with detailed mechanical design.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring machinery placed on the market to be safe; mandates risk assessment, CE/UKCA marking, and a Technical File for machinery above the exclusion thresholds.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete containerised unit as a machinery assembly (HP pump drive train, VFD-controlled motor, dosing pump mechanisms, automated valve actuators, PLC control system); the assembled unit constitutes 'machinery' under the Regulations.
regulatory.designImpact: A machinery risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 must be completed. Guards must be fitted to rotating parts (pump couplings, motor fan). Emergency stop must be provided and accessible. Technical File must be compiled. UKCA Declaration of Conformity required before supply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the machinery assembly; Technical File including risk assessment, design drawings, test records; CE/UKCA marking on the unit nameplate.
regulatory.gapAction: Initiate machinery risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 covering HP pump drive, dosing mechanisms, and automated valves; identify UKCA notified body if Category III machinery assessment is required.

regulatory.name: Safety of Machinery — General Principles for Design — Risk Assessment and Risk Reduction
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard providing the methodology for machinery risk assessment and risk reduction; designated under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Machinery risk assessment for the HP pump drive train, motor coupling, dosing pump mechanisms, and automated valve actuators; demonstrates compliance with Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
regulatory.designImpact: Systematic hazard identification and risk reduction hierarchy (elimination, safeguarding, information) must be applied to all moving parts and high-pressure interfaces. Residual risks must be documented in the Technical File and communicated in the operator manual.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Completed risk assessment document referencing BS EN ISO 12100 methodology, included in the Technical File; operator manual with residual risk warnings.
regulatory.gapAction: Conduct structured risk assessment workshop using BS EN ISO 12100 methodology covering all mechanical hazards and document findings in the Technical File.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (SI 1989/635)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory duty to ensure electrical systems are constructed, maintained, and used so as to prevent danger; applies to all electrical equipment in the workplace.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical systems within the container: HP pump motor (45–75 kW), VFD, PLC/HMI panel, dosing pump motors, lighting, HVAC, and the three-phase mains inlet; applies at every deployment site as a workplace.
regulatory.designImpact: Electrical systems must be designed by a competent person, with adequate protection against overcurrent, earth fault, and isolation. VFD and motor protection must be coordinated. Isolation and lockout/tagout provisions must be designed in. Periodic inspection and testing regime must be established.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical installation certificate (EIC) signed by a competent person; periodic inspection and test records at each deployment; competent-person sign-off on VFD and motor protection coordination study.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a competent electrical engineer to design the internal distribution system and produce the EIC; specify lockout/tagout provisions in the design.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations for fixed electrical installations; the de facto standard demonstrating compliance with EAWR for fixed installations.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal fixed wiring, distribution board, motor starters, VFD wiring, control panel, lighting, and three-phase inlet within the container; demonstrates compliance with Electricity at Work Regulations 1989.
regulatory.designImpact: Internal distribution must comply with shock protection (TN-S or TN-C-S earthing), overcurrent protection, RCD protection on auxiliary circuits, and IP-rated enclosures appropriate to the wet process environment (minimum IP55 in process areas). Cable sizing must account for VFD harmonic loading.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) with schedule of inspections and test results, signed by a qualified person; periodic inspection report at each redeployment.
regulatory.gapAction: Design internal distribution to BS 7671 Chapter 55 (special installations) and engage a qualified electrician to produce the EIC after factory build completion.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime for the safety of electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC placed on the UK market; requires UKCA marking.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The assembled electrical panel (PLC, HMI, VFD, motor starters), HP pump motor, dosing pump motors, and any electrical equipment supplied as part of the unit; all constitute electrical equipment placed on the UK market.
regulatory.designImpact: All electrical equipment must meet the safety objectives of Schedule 2 (protection against hazards from the electrical equipment itself and from hazards it may cause). UKCA marking and Declaration of Conformity required for the panel assembly if assembled in the UK as a new product.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the electrical panel assembly and major electrical components; test evidence against relevant harmonised standards (e.g. BS EN 61439 for switchgear assemblies).
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm UKCA marking obligations for the panel assembly with the panel builder and obtain Declarations of Conformity for all major electrical components.

regulatory.name: Low-Voltage Switchgear and Controlgear Assemblies — General Rules and Power Switchgear Assemblies
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standards for the design and verification of low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies; designated under the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Main electrical distribution panel housing VFD, motor starters, PLC, and protection devices; demonstrates compliance with Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 for the panel assembly.
regulatory.designImpact: Panel must be verified by test or calculation for temperature rise, short-circuit withstand, dielectric properties, and IP rating (IP65 specified). Panel builder must hold design verification records. Internal separation and busbar sizing must be documented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Panel builder's design verification report to BS EN 61439-1/-2; type-test certificates for the panel enclosure; IP65 ingress protection test certificate.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify BS EN 61439-1/-2 compliance to the panel builder at tender stage and require design verification documentation as a contract deliverable.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring apparatus to be designed so that electromagnetic disturbance generated does not exceed levels preventing radio and telecommunications equipment from operating, and that the apparatus has adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — VFD (variable frequency drive) controlling the 45–75 kW HP pump motor is a significant source of conducted and radiated EMC emissions; PLC and HMI are susceptible apparatus; both must comply before placing on the UK market.
regulatory.designImpact: VFD must be specified with integral or external EMC filter to Class C2 or C3 (BS EN 61800-3) for industrial environment. Screened motor cables required. PLC/HMI must meet immunity requirements. EMC assessment must be included in Technical File.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC Declaration of Conformity for the VFD and panel assembly; BS EN 61800-3 compliance certificate from VFD manufacturer; EMC test report or technical construction file assessment.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify VFD with BS EN 61800-3 Category C2/C3 EMC filter at procurement stage and obtain EMC Declaration of Conformity from the VFD supplier.

regulatory.name: UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA) Marking — Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and associated legislation
regulatory.summary: Umbrella UK market-access marking scheme replacing CE marking for products placed on the Great Britain market; applies across multiple product regulations simultaneously.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete containerised unit as a product placed on the GB market; UKCA marking is required under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008, Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, EMC Regulations 2016, and PESR 2016 simultaneously.
regulatory.designImpact: A single UKCA mark may cover multiple directives but each underlying regulation requires its own conformity assessment and Declaration of Conformity. Technical File must be compiled and retained for 10 years. UK Approved Body involvement required where conformity assessment routes mandate third-party assessment (e.g. PESR Category III/IV, Machinery Annex IV).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity referencing all applicable regulations; UKCA mark affixed to the unit nameplate; Technical File retained by the manufacturer for 10 years.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK product compliance manager to coordinate UKCA marking across all applicable regulations and compile the unified Technical File before first unit is placed on the GB market.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (HSWA)
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety statute imposing duties on manufacturers and employers to ensure, so far as reasonably practicable, the health, safety, and welfare of persons at work and affected by work activities.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Design, manufacture, supply, installation, and operation of the unit; Section 6 imposes duties on designers and manufacturers of articles for use at work to ensure they are safe and without risks to health when properly used.
regulatory.designImpact: Safe design must be demonstrated through risk assessment, guarding, safe isolation provisions, and operator documentation. COSHH assessment required for antiscalant, sodium bisulphite, and sodium hypochlorite chemicals used in the process. Manual handling assessment required for membrane element replacement (elements ~15 kg each).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Section 6 safety file including risk assessments, COSHH assessments, manual handling assessment, and operator/maintenance manual; HSE notification if the unit is installed on a construction site under CDM 2015.
regulatory.gapAction: Conduct Section 6 safety review, prepare COSHH assessments for all process chemicals, and produce operator manual with safe-working procedures before first deployment.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/51)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime managing health and safety risks during construction projects; applies to the installation of the unit on construction sites and potentially to civil works associated with deployment.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Construction-site freshwater supply deployments where the unit is installed as part of a notifiable construction project; the founder as designer/supplier has duties under Regulation 9 to eliminate or reduce foreseeable risks during installation, use, and maintenance.
regulatory.designImpact: Design must facilitate safe installation (lifting points, stability during deployment, safe access for connections), safe operation (chemical handling, electrical isolation), and safe maintenance (membrane extraction, filter changeout). Pre-construction information must be provided to the principal designer.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Designer's CDM risk register and pre-construction information pack; lifting plan for container deployment; health and safety file for handover to client.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare CDM designer's risk register covering installation, operation, and maintenance hazards and include lifting point specifications and stability requirements in the mechanical design.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium Metal and Lithium Ion Batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety tests for lithium cells and batteries shipped by road, sea, or air.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — If the unit incorporates a lithium-based UPS or battery backup for the PLC/control system; UN 38.3 + Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG 2009) apply to road transport of lithium batteries. If no lithium battery is included, this row is not applicable.
regulatory.designImpact: Any lithium UPS battery must be sourced with valid UN 38.3 test summary from the cell supplier. ADR dangerous goods documentation required for road shipment. Battery must be secured against movement during transport.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from battery/UPS supplier; ADR transport document for road shipment if lithium battery is included.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether the control system UPS incorporates lithium chemistry; if so, obtain UN 38.3 certificate from the UPS supplier and prepare ADR documentation for road transport.

regulatory.code: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG 2009)
regulatory.name: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1348)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime implementing ADR for road transport of dangerous goods including sodium hypochlorite (Class 8), sodium bisulphite (Class 9), and antiscalant chemicals carried within or with the unit.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Road transport of the unit when process chemical day tanks (sodium hypochlorite, sodium bisulphite, antiscalant) are loaded; these are classified dangerous goods under ADR and require proper shipping documentation, packaging, and driver training.
regulatory.designImpact: Day tanks must be designed to be emptied or isolated before road transport, or the unit must be classified and transported as a dangerous goods vehicle with full ADR compliance. Chemical containment bunding must be integral to the skid design.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: ADR transport documents for each chemical; driver ADR certificate; dangerous goods safety adviser (DGSA) appointment; chemical containment design evidence in the Technical File.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a DGSA to assess the chemical transport obligations and specify whether day tanks must be emptied before road movement; incorporate bunded containment into the skid design.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Specification and Testing — Part 1: General Cargo Containers for General Purposes
regulatory.summary: Structural specification and test standard for ISO series 1 freight containers; the basis for the Container Safety Convention (CSC) plate.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Container shell structural integrity; the original CSC plate is voided once the container shell is structurally modified (side-wall penetrations for feed inlet, brine discharge, permeate outlet, HVAC louvres, and electrical entry). Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is required. The container cannot be stacked under CSC rules after modification without new structural certification.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate is invalidated by side-wall penetrations and internal skid reinforcement. A finite element analysis (FEA) to EN 1993 or equivalent, or a new structural survey by a recognised classification society, is required to certify the modified container for lifting, stacking, and road transport loads.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: FEA report or classification-society structural survey certificate for the modified container; revised lifting and stacking load ratings documented on a replacement data plate.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission FEA of the modified container shell accounting for all penetrations and internal skid loads; engage a classification society (e.g. Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas) for structural re-certification before first deployment.

regulatory.name: Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986 (SI 1986/1078) — Abnormal Load Requirements
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime governing the dimensions and weights of loads on public roads; sets limits for width, height, and overall weight of flatbed lorry loads.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Road transport of the loaded 40-ft container on a flatbed lorry; operating weight 15,000–18,000 kg plus tractor unit; High-Cube option at 2,896 mm height may require Special Types General Order (STGO) notification depending on route.
regulatory.designImpact: High-Cube container height (2,896 mm) plus flatbed deck height (typically 1,200–1,400 mm) gives overall height of approximately 4.1–4.3 m, which may exceed the 4.2 m standard limit on some routes and require abnormal load escort or route survey. Overall weight must be confirmed against axle load limits.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Transport route survey confirming height and weight compliance; STGO notification to Highways England/National Highways if applicable; haulier's abnormal load movement order if required.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm High-Cube container height plus flatbed deck height against UK road height limits and commission a route survey for representative deployment locations; consider standard-height container if High-Cube triggers STGO obligations.

regulatory.code: Water Resources Act 1991 / Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016
regulatory.name: Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 — Brine Discharge Permit
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring an environmental permit for the discharge of brine concentrate to controlled waters (sea, estuary, river, or groundwater).
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Brine (concentrate) discharge at approximately 20.8 m³/h at approximately double feed salinity; discharge to coastal or estuarine waters requires an environmental permit from the Environment Agency (England) or Natural Resources Wales under the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: Brine discharge connection must be designed to accommodate diffuser or dilution requirements specified in the permit. Brine flow metering and sampling ports must be integrated. Discharge point location and pipe specification must be agreed with the Environment Agency before deployment.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Environmental permit for brine discharge from the Environment Agency or Natural Resources Wales; brine dispersion modelling report if required by the regulator; flow metering calibration records.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage the Environment Agency at pre-application stage for each deployment site to determine permit requirements and design the brine discharge connection to accommodate diffuser specifications.

regulatory.code: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH)
regulatory.name: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/2677)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime requiring employers to assess and control exposure to hazardous substances in the workplace; applies to process chemicals used in the desalination unit.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sodium hypochlorite (oxidising, corrosive), sodium bisulphite (irritant, releases SO₂), and antiscalant chemicals used in the pre- and post-treatment trains; operators and maintenance personnel are exposed during chemical handling, dosing system maintenance, and tank refilling.
regulatory.designImpact: Chemical day tanks must be bunded and vented. Dosing system must be enclosed with drip trays. Ventilation must be adequate to prevent SO₂ accumulation from sodium bisulphite. PPE requirements and emergency eyewash must be specified in the operator manual and physically provided with the unit.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: COSHH assessment for each process chemical; safety data sheets (SDS) for all chemicals; ventilation calculation demonstrating adequate dilution; emergency eyewash provision documented in the design.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare COSHH assessments for sodium hypochlorite, sodium bisulphite, and antiscalant; specify bunded day tanks, drip trays, and emergency eyewash in the mechanical design.

regulatory.name: NSF/ANSI 61: Drinking Water System Components — Health Effects
regulatory.summary: US/international standard for health-effects testing of materials and components in contact with drinking water; widely referenced by UK water authorities and insurers for potable-contact components.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — All potable-contact components (permeate-side piping, remineralisation vessel, chlorination dosing components, permeate outlet flange); not UK statutory but referenced in the report as a design requirement and likely required by water authority clients and insurers. UK statutory peer is BS 6920 / WRAS approval.
regulatory.designImpact: Potable-contact components must be sourced from suppliers holding NSF/ANSI 61 certification or equivalent BS 6920/WRAS approval. Dual certification (NSF 61 + BS 6920) preferred for international deployment flexibility.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 61 certification certificates from component suppliers; or BS 6920 / WRAS approval as UK equivalent; supplier declarations referencing certification numbers.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify NSF/ANSI 61 or BS 6920/WRAS approval as a mandatory procurement requirement for all potable-contact components and verify at purchase order stage.

regulatory.name: NSF/ANSI 372: Drinking Water System Components — Lead Content
regulatory.summary: US/international standard specifying lead-free requirements for drinking water system components; referenced in the report as a design requirement.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — All metallic potable-contact components (valves, fittings, permeate outlet flange); not UK statutory but referenced in the report and likely required by water authority clients. UK statutory peer is Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 parametric value for lead.
regulatory.designImpact: All metallic components in the permeate flow path must be specified as lead-free (≤0.25% weighted average lead content). Brass valves and fittings must be DZR or lead-free grade. Supplier declarations of lead content required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 372 certification or supplier lead-content declarations for all metallic potable-contact components; material test certificates (MTC) for stainless steel components confirming alloy composition.
regulatory.gapAction: Add NSF/ANSI 372 or equivalent lead-free requirement to the procurement specification for all metallic permeate-side components and collect supplier declarations at purchase order stage.

regulatory.code: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality (4th Edition)
regulatory.name: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality, 4th Edition
regulatory.summary: International reference guidelines for drinking-water quality used by humanitarian organisations, insurers, and international clients; not UK statutory.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Permeate water quality for disaster-relief and remote-island deployments where local statutory standards may not apply or may be less stringent than WHO guidelines; humanitarian clients (UN agencies, NGOs) will typically specify WHO guideline values as the contractual quality standard.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment train must be validated against WHO guideline values for TDS, microbiological parameters, disinfection by-products, and residual chlorine. Monitoring instrumentation must be capable of measuring WHO-specified parameters.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test report from an accredited laboratory demonstrating compliance with WHO guideline values; client contractual acceptance of water quality data.
regulatory.gapAction: Include WHO guideline values as a design target alongside UK parametric values and specify monitoring instrumentation capable of measuring all relevant WHO parameters.

regulatory.name: UK Biocidal Products Regulation (SI 2013/1506 as retained and amended)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory regime controlling the placing on the market and use of biocidal products; sodium hypochlorite used for post-treatment chlorination is a biocidal product (Product Type 5 — drinking water disinfection).
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sodium hypochlorite used for post-treatment chlorination of permeate; must be a UK BPR-authorised product for drinking water disinfection (Product Type 5) when supplied or used in the UK.
regulatory.designImpact: Sodium hypochlorite specified for the chlorination dosing system must be sourced from a UK BPR-authorised supplier for PT5 use. Dosing concentration and contact time must comply with the authorised product label. Operator training in biocide handling must be documented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UK BPR authorisation certificate for the sodium hypochlorite product (PT5); supplier's authorisation number; operator training records.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm that the specified sodium hypochlorite product holds UK BPR PT5 authorisation for drinking water disinfection and include the authorisation number in the chemical procurement specification.
